usageNotes: This is an extraction of the attached source PDF, not an implementation of Modern 4e rules.
All PDF pages, all class levels, and combat/non-combat/niche indexes are retained, including levels above 10.
Published powers often have only an index entry in this document. Missing definitions are not invented or fetched from another source.
The source's skills, formulas, categories, and wording are retained. Apply Modern 4e adaptations separately.
Page numbers are 1-based PDF page numbers; they coincide with the printed page numbers.
overviewRows and categoryListings are independent observations because the source sometimes disagrees with itself.
Entry level follows the enclosing section. Definition printedLevel preserves the card's label even where it contains an apparent typo.
fullText preserves each printed card and adjacent explanatory material. Parsed fields are convenience fields; verify exact interpretation against fullText and source pages.
PDF text can contain source typos, clipped lines, and imperfect extraction. rawText preserves native extracted page text for cross-checking.
Similar titles are not automatically merged. possibleRelatedEntryIds flags potential naming variants for review.
powerEntries counts indexed class/level/title records, including distinct source spellings that may refer to the same power.

Parsed keywords and categories normalize spacing around hyphens; category parsing also recognizes the source typos 'Non-Coombat' and 'Comba t'. Original wording remains in classificationText and fullText.

Niche implies Combat in reportedCategories and classification comparisons, following the source's definition on page 7. The optional rule allowing Niche picks in non-combat slots is not enabled automatically.
Read the powers array by class, level, reportedCategories, or hasPrintedDefinition. Supporting rules and complete pages are included below.

definitions.name: Friendly Pastor
definitions.fullText:
Friendly Pastor
Cleric Utility 2
You've got a calm and convincing demeanor, trained from
interacting with others in the name of your deity.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Social
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +2 power
bonus to Diplomacy checks. Increase this bonus to a +4
when interacting with people friendly to your church or
deity.

definitions.name: Intimidating Sermon
definitions.fullText:
Intimidating Sermon
Cleric Utility 2
Your fire and brimstone speech strikes the fear of your deity into
those who fear the wrath of your god's power.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Social
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +3 power
bonus to Intimidation checks. If you have been able to speak
to the target or targets of your intimidation attempt for at
last 5 minutes, increase this bonus to a +5.
Special: This may not affect enemies who are servants to
deities directly opposed to your deity.

definitions.name: Lesser Religious Rites
definitions.fullText:
Lesser Religious Rites
Cleric Utility 2
With practice or experience you've learned to be ready to cast divi
rituals with minimum preparation, and thus you always keep some
spare components for them just in case.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine, Ritual
Free Action
Personal
Trigger : You are performing a Religion, Nature, or Heal ritual
of 5th level or lower.
Effect: You cast the ritual without expending any of the ritual's
gold piece component cost (any focus item must still meet
the minimum cost). You and any assisting allies get a -2
penalty to any skill required or affected by the ritual until the
effect of the ritual is complete..

definitions.name: Preacher Power
definitions.fullText:
Preacher Power
Cleric Utility 2
You manifest minor miracles that enhance your presence so that
others listen to your word and know you speak for your god.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Divine , Cantrip
Minor Action
Personal
Point: Description.
Effect: You create one of the following magical effects on
yourself. They last until the end of your next turn:
•
Your voice booms up to three times as loud.
•
You alter the appearance of your eyes.
•
You appear, to others' eyes, to grow or shrink in size
by up to a foot.
Sustain Standard: You sustain the effect and you may add
another one of the effects as well. You may only have up to
three of these effects ongoing at a time, and you may sustain
all of them at once with this sustain action.

definitions.name: Confession
definitions.fullText:
Confession
Cleric Utility 6
In your past, followers would look to you for absolution, and even
now, you are able to use that skill to convince peole to confide in y
their deepest and darkest secrets
.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Social
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, you get a +5 bonus to
your next skill check (usually Diplomacy or Intimidation) to
get a creature that you can speak the language of and are
conversing with to confess a secret to you. They must be
friendly or neutral, and cannot be hostile.

definitions.name: Dark Whispers
definitions.fullText:
Dark Whispers
Cleric Utility 6
You cause the shadows of a deep cave, a flickering candle, or
something else, to whisper from the deep.
Daily + Non-Combat, Ritual, Exploration, Divine, Shadow,
Zone
Minor Action
Ranged 150 (750 ft)
Target: One square of shadow within total darkness or dim
light
Effect: The target square of shadow becomes a zone through
which you can communicate. You must utilize some sort of
darkness, including the shadow of a person or object. Your
words emerge from the darkness as a clear whisper, absent
any identifying features of your voice. You can choose to
whisper to someone in or adjacent to the zone. You can also
hear anyone in or adjacent to the zone as well. Their
responses emerge as clear whispers.
Once the effect is active, you don't need to have line of
sight or effect to the zone to commnicate back and forth or
to sustain the power.
The whispers emerging from the shadows or the
whispered responses back to you can be overheard by a
Perception check (DC 15 + your level + your Wisdom
modifier) by those who are close.
Sustain Minor: You sustain the effect until the end of your
next turn. This power can be sustained up to 1 hour per
level.

definitions.name: Thaumaturgy
definitions.fullText:
Thaumaturgy
Cleric Utility 6
Your manifest a minor wonder, a glimpse of the power you channe
on behalf of your deity.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Divine , Cantrip
Standard Action
Ranged 5
Point: Description.
Effect: You create one of the following magical effects within
range. They last until the end of your next turn:
•
You cause flames to flicker, brighten, or dim.
•
You cause harmless tremors in the ground.
•
You create an instanteous sound that originates
from a point of your choice within range, such as a
rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous
whispers. It cannot imitate the voice or sound of
anyone specific, or of a specific language, but it can
approximate the voice or sound of a type of
creature.
•
You instaneously cause an unlocked door or window
to fly open or slam shut .
Sustain Standard: You sustain the effect and you may add
another one of the effects as well. You may only have up to
three of these effects ongoing at a time, and you may sustain
all of them at once with this sustain action.

definitions.name: Theologian’s Knowledge
definitions.fullText:
Theologian’s Knowledge
Cleric Utility 6
You recall knowledge from your days of religious schooling,
studying dusty tomes, old myths, and religious tradition.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Gathering Information
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You are making a knowledge check (that is not a
Monster Knowledge check).
Effect: You may roll with Religion instead of the original skill
and use that for the result of the triggering knowledge check.
If it is related to your deity, you get a +2 bonus (DM has the
final say on whether the knowledge relates to your deity).

definitions.name: Church Attendants
definitions.fullText:
Church Attendants
Cleric Utility 10
Your reputation precedes you, causing nearby churches to rush to
help you when they see you. Or perhaps, you just have a nice face
and a persuasive tongue.
Daily + Non-Combat, Social, Urban
No Action
Personal
Effect: While in an area with a church or temple dedicated to
your deity and not hostile or unfriendly to you, you may
recruit up to 2 attendants to help you out in non -combat
scenarios. For example, they can hlep get your horse ready,
carry your things, deliver m essages, go shopping for you, aid
another inskill checks outside of combat (they have your
stats), etc.
They will only help you out while you are in the area
with the house of worship, or the immediate surrounding
area. They will avoid danger where possible, and may not
join you in places where that can't be avoided (example: they
may accompany you on a mai n road between cities, but they
will probably stay and hide at the entrance to a dungeon,
and will probably leave when you get to the next city ).

definitions.name: Conditional Favor
definitions.fullText:
Conditional Favor
Cleric Utility 10
You swear the target to an oath and
grant them a powerful divine
blessing, empowering them for as long as they obey your
commandment.
Daily + Non-Combat , Ritual, Binding, Divine
Standard Action
Melee Touch
Cast Time: 5 minutes
Target: One willing creature
Effect: Expend another power or ritual you have that can
target the same target as this power. You must elicit a
promise or warning against a behavior from the target. If
they violate that oath or prohibition while this is in effect, the
expended benefit of the ex pended power or ritual is undone.
(If it was a healing spell, for example, the hit point damage or
a removed condition is return immediately.)
Conditional favor recognizes the spirit of the
condition and doesn't trigger a violation due to unintended
consquences or circumstances that the subject could not
predict with her current knowledge of the situation. (For
example, touching a disguised royal prince you were
forbidden from touching won't trigger a violation.) The
subject knows beforehand whether an action will cause it to
lose the paired spell's benefit. The effect of this power also
ends at the end of your next extended rest.

definitions.name: Divine Mediator
definitions.fullText:
Divine Mediator
Cleric Utility 10
You exhibit the traits of a messenger from your deity, giving you a
certain authority when speaking to creatures associated with it.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Social , Divine
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, you get a +5 bonus to
interacting socially with immortals and other monster races
or types related to your deity (usually either supported by or
directly opposed by). If you have a Channel Divinity or other
Divine power rel ated to undead, you may also apply this
bonus when socially interacting with the undead. You also
gain a language during this encounter if needed. If you do not
worship one of these gods, you and your DM choose the type
and/or gained language related to yo ur deity together.

definitions.name: Religious Rites
definitions.fullText:
Religious Rites
Cleric Utility 10
You've become even better at always having the proper componen
for rituals and improvising them when you can't.
Daily + Non-Combat, Ritual, Divine
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You are performing a Religion, Nature, or Heal ritual
of 9th level or lower.
Effect: You cast the ritual without expending any of the ritual's
gold piece component cost (any focus item must still meet
the minimum cost). Instead, ou must expend one healing
surge, and you double the time to cast the ritual. If you roll a
20 on the ritual ski ll check, you regain the expended healing
surge. If the ritual doesn't require a skill check, you can make
one anyway when using it to try to gain this benefit. This
power cannot be used on any ritual that raises the dead, or
creates or enchants an item.

definitions.name: Clairovoyant Vision
definitions.fullText:
Clairovoyant Vision
Cleric Utility 1 6
Your deity gives you a vision of a nearby place in your time of need
Daily + Non-Combat, Divination, Divine
Standard Action
Ranged 40
Special: Line-of-sight and line -of-effect not required
Target: One square
Effect: You get a still 3D picture in your head as if you were
floating in the target square at the moment in time you
finished casting this power. You receive the image as if you
had darkvision, low -light vision, and time was frozen. You
can observe this image fo r about 10 seconds, you can turn
around, but can't move forward or backward, up, or down.
You also receive about 10 seconds of sound to accompany

definitions.name: Charitable Impulse
definitions.fullText:
Charitable Impulse
Cleric Utility 22
You cast a spell that makes a creature more charitable, wanting to
help others over everyone else.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine , Charm, Implement
Standard Action
Ranged 5
Target: One creature
Attack: Wisdom vs Will
Hit: The targeted creature attempts to perform at least one of
the following priorities on each of their turns until the effect
ends, they make their saving throw, or they go through all of
the priorities, starting with the first one. The target continues
to perform a priority until they can no longer fulfill its
demands, at which point they move to the next priority.
The target is considered Dominated (save ends)
during this time for the purposes of other effects, however
they while under this effect they can use all of their normal
actions in a turn, but they must try to use at least one action
to complete the priorit y they are on to the best of their
ability. The target cannot take opportunity attacks but will
try to defend themselves. If the target is attacked, the effect
ends.
+
1st Priority: Heal injured creatures within the
target's speed, beignning with the closest, using
what they have on hand.
+
2nd Priority: The target uses beneficial powers
and/or items on the closest creature within their
speed.
+
3rd Priority: The target gives away their non -worn
posesssions, starting with their money, to the closest
creatures within their speed. If the creature does not
accept the item or money, they will attempt to move
to the other nearest creature to give them the
charity.
+
4th Priority: The target gives away their remaining
posessions (armor, boots, cloaks, etc.) to the closest
creature within their speed. If the creature does not
accept the item, they will attempt to move to the
other nearest creature to give them the items .

Imbue with Blessed
Cleric Utility 22
Spells
Becoming god-like yourself, you give others a sliver of the power yo
inherit from your deity.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine, Binding , Ritual
Standard Action
Melee Touch
Target: One willing ally
Cast Time: 1 hour
Effect: The target ally gains access to one of your Cleric
prayers. You cannot use this power again until they cast that
prayer or until you take back the power as a free action. You
also take the power back if the target dies. It must be an At -
Will or Encounter power. The power gains an enhancement
bonus as if they were using your main weapon or implement
that you would use with that power, at the time you imbue
the target.

definitions.name: Sermon
definitions.fullText:
Sermon
Cleric Utility 22
You entrance the crowd with an interesting speech on a topic you
can pontificate on for hours on end.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine, Social, Zone
Standard Action
Close Burst 60
Target: One or more non -hostile creatures in the burst
Attack: Wisdom vs Will. You may roll against the enemy with
the highest Will and count that against everyone in the same
area.
Hit: Each creature in the burst stands or sits still while they
listen to you speak, maybe giving the occasional response.
They take a -5 penalty to Perception checks while they
remain focused on you . Any potential hostile action in the
area (including drawing a sword, casting a spell, aiming a
ranged weapon, yelling a threat, etc.) or rolling of initiative
ends the effect.
Sustain Standard: You sustain the effect until the end of your
next turn. You can sustain this power for up to 2 hours. After
the first hour, you must remake the attack roll in order to
sustain this power, and the penalty is reduced to a -2.
Miss: Each creature in the area is briefly distracted by you, but
they don't feel compelled to stay and listen to the whole talk.
They get a -5 penalty to Perception checks until the end of
your next turn, but this power can't be sustained.

definitions.fullText:
Are You Not Entertained?!
Fighter Utility 2
You can get the audience on your side, even while performing
violence, through your charm, bravado, hype, or general likeability
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Social
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You reduce an enemy to 0 hit points or less.
Effect: All Diplomacy checks to influence any and all creatures
in the audience after the combat encounter towards a more
positive attitude to you get a +5 bonus. The audience counts
all creatures who can perceive the battle but are not
participating in it (not as allies or enemies).
This bonus lasts until you successfully raise their
attitude, complete a social encounter, or until the next
extended rest (which ever is sooner).

definitions.name: I’ll Give You One
definitions.fullText:
I’ll Give You One
Fighter Utility 2
You admit you may have pissed somebody off now or in the past,
but try to let out some of the tension by letting them take out thei
anger on you with one good blow.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial , Social
Standard Action
Personal
Target: One creature you are talking with that is angry or
displeased at you or an ally
Effect: You let the enemy make a free attack on you. It
automatically hits, but you have resistance 5 to the damage.
Afterwards, gain a +5 bonus to any Diplomacy checks with
the target and their allies in the vicinity until the end of the
next turn, and you may in crease their attitude as if a past
event which may have enraged or displeased them did not
happen.
Level 11: The damage resistance increases by your
Constitution modifier.
Special : The DM may rule that this can only be used on certain
creatures. A fellow mercenary or an insulted drunkard may
appreciate the gesture, but an ambassador negotiating in a
fancy ballroom will find it uncouth and not appreciate it.

definitions.name: Old War Buddy
definitions.fullText:
Old War Buddy
Fighter Utility 2
You look around with recognition at this place. "Well I'll be, this is
where my fencing master's other best student moved to. Come on,
I know them, they'll be at the nicest tavern, and they still owe me a
favor for saving their butt. Our old master stil
l thinks it was I who
broke his prized tea set. If someone can tell us what's going on her
they can."
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Social , Gathering Information
Free Action
Personal
Special: The first time you use this power you may designate a
nearby populated settlement as having a contact. Work with
the DM to decide the nature of this contact. The contact must
be related to your past as a fighter. Every time you use this
power after the first time, use the below effect.
Effect: You are easily able to find the chosen contact if you are
in the area they frequent, or are easily able to find out if
they've moved on from the area. If they or someone else has
made it difficult for some reason (for example, they are in
hiding, were kidnapped, they're a criminal, or you chose
someone extremely important and busy, like an old noble
you swore your allegiance to) you gain a bonus to any checks
to find hints in the area of their location, well -being, or to
bypass the people or politics to find them equal to your
Wisdom modifier + 2.
The contact will only help you with information. You
gain +5 bonus to knowledge checks for information they
would reasonably know while talking to them if they are
amenable to help.
Special : You may choose this ability again even if you have
already learned it to gain additional contacts . You may also
choose a new contact if an old one dies or becomes
inaccessible.
Old War Buddy Inspiration
/Examples
What does it mean that the contact relates to your past
as a fighter? Here are some examples of some contacts
for the Old War Buddy fighter power: a fellow soldier in
your platoon, a trainer, mentor, superior officer,
blacksmith who made your weapon or armor, old rival
in the pit or arena, the second in your duels, a former
trainee or mentee who has gone off to do their own
thing, etc.

ruleFields.text: You are easily able to find the chosen contact if you are in the area they frequent, or are easily able to find out if they've moved on from the area. If they or someone else has made it difficult for some reason (for example, they are in hiding, were kidnapped, they're a criminal, or you chose someone extremely important and busy, like an old noble you swore your allegiance to) you gain a bonus to any checks to find hints in the area of their location, well -being, or to bypass the people or politics to find them equal to your Wisdom modifier + 2. The contact will only help you with information. You gain +5 bonus to knowledge checks for information they would reasonably know while talking to them if they are amenable to help.

ruleFields.label: Special
ruleFields.text: You may choose this ability again even if you have already learned it to gain additional contacts . You may also choose a new contact if an old one dies or becomes inaccessible. Old War Buddy Inspiration /Examples What does it mean that the contact relates to your past as a fighter? Here are some examples of some contacts for the Old War Buddy fighter power: a fellow soldier in your platoon, a trainer, mentor, superior officer, blacksmith who made your weapon or armor, old rival in the pit or arena, the second in your duels, a former trainee or mentee who has gone off to do their own thing, etc.

definitions.name: Terror of the Heel
definitions.fullText:
Terror of the Heel
Fighter Utility 2
You can get the audience to dislike with an unnatural intensity.
They boo, jeer, and gasp in terror at your fighting style or the thing
you say.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Social , Deception
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You reduce an enemy to 0 hit points or less.
Effect: You get a +3 bonus to Bluff checks to influence the
audience during this encounter. You get a +3 bonus to all
Intimidation checks to influence the audience after the
combat encounter. The audience counts all creatures who
can perceive the battle but are not participating in it (not as
allies or enemies).
You may also give anyone who was on the other side
of the battle (or appeared to be to the audience) a +3 bonus
to Diplomacy checks to influence this same audience
positively.
This bonus lasts until you successfully intimidate
them, complete a social encounter, or until the end of your
next extended rest.

definitions.name: Swords to Pitons
definitions.fullText:
Swords to Pitons
Fighter Utility 2
You throw a weapon or two into the side of a cliff or wall to give
something to hold onto, to either help your ally climb or stop fallin
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial , Exploration , Weapon
Free Action
Ranged 15
Requirement: You must be wielding a light blade, heavy
blade, axe, or spear.
Trigger: An ally in the burst is making a skill check to jump, or
starts flying.
Effect: You throw a weapon you are wielding of one of the
required types into the vertical surface near the ally. If they
are falling, they catch it and stay at that height instead of
falling. If they failed the Athletics check to climb, they can
reroll that check and use the higher result.
Special: If you are wielding two weapons of the required types,
you may throw both. They land next to each other and
provide a useful place for the target's feet, provided they can
balance on them. They may roll their next Climb check using
Acrobatics instead of At hletics and/or Dexterity instead of
Strength if they want. Their next skill check to climb or
reduce falling damage also gets a +2 bonus .

Fighter Utility 6
You have gotten used to the balance of your polearm, able to hold
in the proper place and way to help you cross tight ropes, ledges,
rickety bridges, and more with greater ease.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Martial, Exploration , Weapon

Personal

your next turn, you gain a +4 bonus to Acrobatics checks to
balance on it. You get a -2 penalty to attacks with your
polearm during this time.
Sustain Minor: The effect and penalty persist until the end of
your next turn.

definitions.fullText:
Cutting Symbol of Renown
Fighter Utility 2
You leave a sign of your presence, usually a symbol you've cut into
wall or floor, to further spread your legend to those who pass by la
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Social, Renown, Creation,
Urban, Weapon
Standard Action
Melee Weapon
Requirement : You must be wielding a light blade, heavy
blade, spear, axe, or whip.
Trigger: You have completed an encounter.
Effect: At the end of your next extended rest, your reputation
begins to spread. After that, as long as you are in the local
area where this power was used, you gain a d20 reputation
die. Whenever you or an ally in your party makes a social
check, you may leverage your reputation to roll the
reputation die, and use the higher result.
If you use the die for a social check you were
making, you get a +2 bonus to the second roll. For any local
area you are in, you may only have one reputation die at a
time.
Renown: If used after a special encounter and you are using
renown rules, this may boost your renown an extra +1 or
rolls related to your renown an extra +2 . A special encounter
may be a boss fight, or a particular epic skill challenge,
explosions, something in front of a crowd, etc.
Notes on Cutting Symbol of Renown
It’s best if the reputation die used relates to the
triggering encounter.
For example, if you were in a lair, dungeon, or settlement
ruled by a particular faction or enemy, or completed an
encounter against htem in some way, you could use the
reputation die to reroll an in
timidation check when
interacting with that faction or their allies. Or you could
use it to reroll a Diplomacy check when interacting with
people opposed to or oppressed by those enemies.
If you were doing a quest for someone, you could use the
reputation die to reroll a Diplomacy check when
interacting with the person who gave you the quest, as
well as their friends and allies. If the quest giver was a
talkative merchant, it could even be used with any of
their customers.

definitions.name: Shield Slide
definitions.fullText:
Shield Slide
Fighter Utility 6
You see an incline and use this opportunity to slide down the hill lik
a board.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Martial, Weapon
Free Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be wielding a shield.
Effect: You may slide downhill of the ground you are on. You
shift up to your speed downhill, but you must end your
movement at the end of the ramp, stairs, or incline you are
going down.
You may also choose to jump at the end of your
shift. You gain a +1 bonus for each square you shifted and it
counts as a running jump.

definitions.name: Stabilizing Shield
definitions.fullText:
Stabilizing Shield
Fighter Utility 6
You hold up a falling building, debris from a collapsing cave
-in, the
snow from an avalanche, hail, or even a falling dragon.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial , Weapon
Immediate Interrupt
Close Burst 1
Requirement: You must be wielding a shield.
Trigger: Something falls on you or your allies that would cause
damage or loss of a healing surge.
Special: You may shift up to your Dexterity modifier squares
first before using the rest of this power.
Effect: Reduce the damage from the triggering effect to you
and adjacent allies by your Strength modifier + Constitution
modifier + 2. If you would lose a healing surge from this
effect, you do not lose that healing surge.
Level 11 : Strength modifier + Constitution modifier + 5
Level 21 : Strength modifier + Constitution modifier + 10
Sustain Standard : Make a DC 15 Endurance check. If you
succeed, you continue to reduce any damage from effects
related to the triggering event until the end of your next turn.
The DC of this check increases by 5 every time you sustain
this power.

strong cutting motion to an item
, like a lock or some chains.

Melee Weapon
Requirement: You must be wielding two weapons that are a
combination of light blades and heavy blades. .
Target: One object or part of an object that is small enough to
fit between your two weapons .

make an attack against the object. If making a Strength
check, add a +15 bonus to it. If making an attack against the
object, use the following: Strength vs AC, 3[W] (main hand) +
3[W] (off-hand) + Streng th modifier damage.

definitions.name: Flail Pull
definitions.fullText:
Flail Pull
Fighter Utility 10
You tie your weapon around something heavy you want dragged,
like your haul in a too-large chest, or something you want broken,
like the bars of a jail cell.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial, Exploration , Weapon
Minor Action
Melee 2
Requirement: You must be wielding a flail.
Target: One object that has a part narrow enough your flail
can be wrapped around it.
Effect: You wrap your flail around a part of the target. Until the
end of the encounter, while the flail is wrapped around the
object you cannot use it for anything else, but triple your
drag capacity. In addition, you get a +10 bonus to your
Strength checks to break the target.

some of your downtime honing them while still getting the benefit
of a rest.

Standard Action
Personal
Requirement : You must be taking a short or extended rest. .
Target: One armor or shield.

or shield gains a +1 bonus to AC.

Reflex.
If you target an armor, choose a physical activity (ex:
climbing, swimming, balancing, jumping, etc). It gets one less
armor check penalty when doing that specific activity.

definitions.fullText:
Polearm Platform
Fighter Utility 1
You throw your spear into the side of a wall, giving an opportunity
for an ally to grab a hold of it, and if they are dexterous enough,
balance on it and rain down hell from above.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial, Exploration , Weapon
Minor Action
Ranged 20
Requirement: You must be wielding a polearm or spear.
Target: One square with a wall or similar vertical surface.
Effect: You throw your weapon at the target. It can be
removed with a standard action. That square becomes able
to be climbed without a check. It can also be stood on, but it
requires an Acrobatics check with a hard DC of your level.
They get a +2 bonus to this ch eck if you are able to wedge it
between two vertical surfaces where it can be more stable.
They can also swing on it to use an Acrobatics check
to jump horizontally from that square (instead of Athletics). If
they do, it counts as a running jump.
Weapon : If the weapon is magic, you can remove it at any
time during your turn as a free action without a check, and it
goes straight to your hand.

they will became distracted either by rage or fear.

followers if they are a leader, after this encounter, you gain a

definitions.name: Blade Brake
definitions.fullText:
Blade Brake
Fighter Utility 16
Before you can fall to your death, you stick your blade into the tree
and use it to slow your momentum, splitting the tree, but landing
harmlessly on the ground below
.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial , Weapon
Immediate Reaction
Personal
Trigger: You are falling down a space adjacent to a wall .
Requirement : When falling next to a light material (like a
cloth sail, a rug, a hide tarp, etc) you must be wielding a light
blade, heavy blade, or axe. When falling next to anything
harder, you must be wielding a heavy blade, a two -handed
axe, or two light blades or o ne-handed axes..
Effect: Do not count the distance you fell up to this point as
part of your fall for the sake of falling damage. In addition, as
long as you are falling next to this wall or obstacle, do not
count that distance as part of the fall for the sake of falling
damage. Y ou or DM may choose if the object is damaged by
this.

Renown

representing you into a wall or floor, it brings fear and wariness in
anyone who sees it.

blade, spear, axe, or whip.

action.

faction.

definitions.name: Floating Defensive Spin
definitions.fullText:
Floating Defensive Spin
Fighter Utility 16
You spin your spear like a helicopter, both letting you slightly hove
and create a defensive zone.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Stance, Weapon
Minor Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be wielding a spear, staff, or polearm.
Effect: While in this stance, you and adjacent allies gain a +2
power bonus to AC and Reflex against traps, hazards, and
other non-creature sources.
In addition, while you are falling, you slowly glide
downwards instead. If you are falling and in this stance, you
may choose to gain a fly speed of 1, but at the end of each of
your turns, you fall up to 3 squares .
Weapon : If you are wielding a reach weapon or two
weapons, extend the range of your AC and Reflex bonuses by
1 square. Also, you do not take falling damage for falling 3 or
less squares.

from moving (ex: bracing a door, stopping a runaway cart,
preventing a moving wall trap from moving, etc).

definitions.fullText:
Reinforcing Rest
Fighter Utility 16
You spend some downtime adding some pieces to some armor
where you can, to make it temporarily tougher.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Creation, Rest
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You are taking a short or extended rest.
Target: If taking a short rest, choose one armor or shield you or
an ally resting with you is holding. If taking an extended rest,
choose one armor or shield for each ally resting with you.
Effect: You and each ally resting with you gains damage
resistance equal to 5+ your Wisdom modifier as long as they
ahve the target armor or shield equipped. This disappears
after the first time they are hit by an attack or at the end of
your next short rest. If they are also holding a targeted shield,
they may gain this benefit a second time in the same combat
encounter.

definitions.name: Shackling Flail
definitions.fullText:
Shackling Flail
Fighter Utility 16
You tie the enemy up with your flail so that a simple tug chokes
them, sends spikes into flesh, the chain rips skin, the weight starts
crushing bone, or it does something else very comfortable.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial , Weapon
Standard Action
Melee 1
Requirement: You must be wielding a flail or whip.
Target: One helpless creature
Effect: The target is restrained and grabbed by your weapon
until you retrieve it or they escape. The weapon cannot be
used for anything else until that time. When you may move,
you may immediately afterwards you move them adjacent to
you as well.
The Acrobatics DC to escape is a hard DC of your
level. The Strength check to break free is DC 30 if your
weapon is iron or a softer material, DC 40 if it's a harder
material (like adamantine or mithril), 45 if it's magical, and
50 if it's both magical and a harder material. Also increase
the DC by +5 if you are a higher or equal level to them.
However, if they are grabbed by you, whenever they
attempt to break free, escape, teleport, or move away from
you, you may tug at the flail as an Immediate Interrupt to do
this attack: Strength + 2 vs Fortitude; Hit: 2d6 damage. The
enemy cannot move or tele port this turn and they get a
penalty to escape attempts equal to the damage dealt.

definitions.name: Shielding Barricade
definitions.fullText:
Shielding Barricade
Fighter Utility 16
With a mighty throw, you hammer your shield into the ground to
create better cover to hide the approach allies or attract attention
and provide a distraction. Although it does take an additional goo
hit to really stay in there.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial , Weapon
Standard Action
Ranged 5
Requirement: You must be wielding a heavy shield.
Target: One square
Effect: You create a low wall in the target square that provides
full cover and total concealment to anyone in it hiding
behind the shield until the end of your next turn.
If you or an ally are hiding behind the shield and not
in combat, they may use a free action during their turn to
bump it, reflecting light from it and blinding any creature
who was staring at it until the end of their next turn, as long
as there is another light source in the area.
Sustain Standard: The shield stays in the ground until you
remove it as a standard action. You or an ally must be in the
same square or adjacent to the target the shield is to sustain
it. If in combat, a DC 20 Strength check is rewquired.

definitions.name: Shield Thrower
definitions.fullText:
Shield Thrower
Fighter Utility 16
You are able to throw your shield with such skill it can bounce off
things and return back to you.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial , Weapon
Standard Action
Ranged 10
Requirement: You must be wielding a heavy shield.
Target: One square
Effect: You throw your shield at the target. You may apply any
ranged power that uses your shield as if it was used from that
square.
Afterwards, it bounces harmlessly off objects and
creatures within 12 squares of you and returns to your
hands. It can't cause any additional effects or damage during
this time, except for one of the following if you wish :
+
The shield has a simple interaction with one object
in this path as if you were there (open or close a
door, lock a door, pull a lever, push or pull an object,
etc.)
+
You may have the shield stay lodged in one object,
such as to bar a door, keep a curtain open, etc.
+
You may have a creature catch the shield .
+
You can cut an object that could be cut with a
mundane knife, like a rope.

definitions.name: Summon Martial Squires
definitions.fullText:
Summon Martial Squires
Fighter Utility 16
You have attracted squires to help you out through your reputatio
deeds, mentorship, subordinate officers, etc. They may normally
follow from a near but safe distance, or are stationed in the area,
if you require their help they will come ride for yo
u at a moment's
notice.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial , Social
Standard Action
Close Burst 5
Effect: You summon up to 3 companions to your position.
They can help you with mundane tasks (holding things,
moving things, cleaning, delivering messages, tc.) with only
general direction needed, taking their own initaitive withour
using your actions until the ne xt extended rest. They match
your ability bonuses for non -combat purposes. Once
committed to an out-of-combt task they will not help out in
combat.
You can also use this power to call them to battle,
but they count as minions and use your actions to act. If 2 of
3 died, you lose a healing surge and the 3rd will run away if
able. If they weren’t summoned and traveling with you
before the battle, they don’t show up until the combat
encounter has ended.
Standard Action: Melee 1; Strength vs AC; 1d10 + Strength
modifier damage.
Move Action: Move up to 3 of your squires. They have the
same base speed as you.

weak point along your foe's weapon,
and with perfect skill and luck,
you find it - shattering it.

hammer, staff, or pick.

definitions.fullText:
Weapon Smith’s Rest
Fighter Utility 16
You make some temporary improvements of the weapons for you
and your allies. It may take a few practice swings, but once they g
the hang of it, they will realize the improvements.

Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You are taking a short rest.
Target: Choose one melee weapon.
Effect: During the next combat encounter before your next
short or extended rest, each ally who wields a targeted
weapon marks down whenever they miss an attack. After
the second miss, any target weapon they wield deals an extra
+2 damage until the end of the encounter. The damage is
dealt even on a miss.

through almost anything with a single blow.

automatically dealing enough damage to the object to break
it.

of a special material (like adamantine), you can target any
mundane object made of metal, too.

While there exists the stereotype of the grim paladin, many adopt
interpersonal skills and are quite friendly, a result of the empathy
required to talk to the people that you are required to protect.

to Diplomacy and Insight checks when interacting with
people friendly to your church or deity. You also gain a +2
power bonus when interacting with someone you have
protected or attempted to protect or advocate for this
encounter. These two bonuses can stack.

extended rest unless you make a Hard DC Endurance check
with a -5 penalty. After every extended rest you make, you
get an increasing, stacking +5 bonus to this check.

definitions.name: Providential Meeting
definitions.fullText:
Providential Meeting
Paladin Utility 6
Often when others call out to the gods for help, you are the one w
arrives. By divine providence, a person you have helped in the past
appears before you once again.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine, Social, Urban
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement : You are in a populated settlement and outside
of combat.
Special : The first time you use this power, choose a contact
that lives or is traveling through the area. The contact must
be related to your past as a paladin, usually someone you've
saved or helped before, and they must be a mundane NPC,
without great power or in fluence (not an adventurer or hero,
think the equivalent of an average NPC villager). You may
only have one contact this way. Once you have chosen a
contact, you cannot change it until that contact is removed
from the story or you choose to retrain this po wer.
Effect: The DM bends the circumstances such that by pure
luck you run into the old contact you have already chosen for
this power. Roll a d20. On a 10 or lower, they will also have
a problem or request that you or your allies can help with.
Until the end of your next extended rest, you gain a
+2 bonus to the next Diplomacy checks you make when
talking with this contact to get their help for something.
In addition, sometimes you may need to roll a
knowledge check for your contact to see if they can answer a
question you are asking them. If you do, use your own stats
for them and you gain a +2 bonus to the next knowledge
check you make for your contact, a s long as it is information
they would reasonably know. Both of these bonuses increase
to a +4 if you have taken care of their problem.
Special: You may choose this power again even if you have
already learned it to gain access to another contact.

The contact must be related to your past as a paladin, usually someone you've saved or helped before, and they must be a mundane NPC, without great power or in fluence (not an adventurer or hero, think the equivalent of an average NPC villager). You may only have one contact this way. Once you have chosen a contact, you cannot change it until that contact is removed from the story or you choose to retrain this po wer.

ruleFields.label: Effect
ruleFields.text: The DM bends the circumstances such that by pure luck you run into the old contact you have already chosen for this power. Roll a d20. On a 10 or lower, they will also have a problem or request that you or your allies can help with. Until the end of your next extended rest, you gain a +2 bonus to the next Diplomacy checks you make when talking with this contact to get their help for something. In addition, sometimes you may need to roll a knowledge check for your contact to see if they can answer a question you are asking them. If you do, use your own stats for them and you gain a +2 bonus to the next knowledge check you make for your contact, a s long as it is information they would reasonably know. Both of these bonuses increase to a +4 if you have taken care of their problem.

ruleFields.label: Special
ruleFields.text: You may choose this power again even if you have already learned it to gain access to another contact.

With the power of an unholy speech, you call forth to a spirit from
beyond the grave to return and answer your questions.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine, Shadow, Gathering
Information, Rest
Standard Action
Personal

more. During this time, you and the corpse are able to speak
and understand a new language called Dread Speech that
helps compel them to answer your questions. You gain a +2
bonus to Diplomacy checks and Insight checks with them
during this conversation.

Divine Shattering
Paladin Utility 10
Your weapon glows with an awesome might as you strike down th
weapons and barriers erected by your cursed foes.
.

Minor Action
Personal
Target: One object.
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, triple your Strength
modifier when using Strength checks to destroy the target, or
deal 3 times damage to the target. If the object is magical,
ignore any damage resistance it might have.
If the object is not an artifact and can be affected by
the Disenchant ritual, then you may choose to expend a
healing surge to immediately destroy the object or obstacle,
but you do not regain this power for a number for long rests
equal to the level of the magic item that you destroyed.

Lean On Me
Paladin Utility 10
You infuse yourself with divine energy and rush to an ally's aid.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine
No Action
Personal
Trigger : An ally fails a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution skill
check during a group skill check or skill challenge.

check as them with a power bonus equal to your Wisdom or
Charisma modifier. If you succeed, their roll counts as a
success instead of a failure. If you fail, their roll still counts as
a failure but your roll does not.

definitions.name: Summon Noble Squire
definitions.fullText:
Summon Noble Squire
Paladin Utility 10
You have attracted a companion squire to help you through your
reputation, deeds in the story, oaths, mentorship, etc. They may
normally follow from a near but safe distance, or are stationed in
the area, but if you require their help they will come ride f
or you at a
moment's notice.
Daily + Non-Combat
Minor Action
Personal
Special : The first time you use this power, choose one of your
ability scores.
Effect: You summon up a companion squire to your nearby
area. They can help you with mundane tasks (holding things,
moving things, cleaning, delivering messages, getting a
mount ready or bringing it over, etc) with only general
direction needed, taking their own i nitiative to the best of
their ability without using your actions until your next long
rest, or until they are summoned again and given new orders.
They match the ability score chosen the first time you used
this power but with an additional +2 bonus, and they get an
11 to all of their other ability scores. Once committed to an
out-of-combat task, they will not help out in combat.
You can also use this power to call them to battle
adjacent to you, but they count as a minion, are not damaged
by missed attacks, and use your actions to act.
Standard Action: Melee 1; Strength vs AC; 1d8 + Strength
modifier damage.
Move Action: Move your squire up to 5 squares.

Calming Presence
Paladin Utility 1 6
Your calming voices makes everyone nearby more comfortable.
Encounter + Non-Combat , Social
Standard Action
Aura 5
Requirement : You are out of combat.
Target: Each creature in the burst.
Effect: Any changes in attitude resulting from previously failed
social skill checks this encounter are undone. In addition, all
targets become calm, reasonable, and logical, granting a +2
power bonus to Diplomacy and Nature checks made against
them until the end of your next turn. These effects also end
as soon as an aggressive action is taken (such as a weapon
being drawn) or initiative is rolled.

slide the ally a number of squares equal to yoru Strength

definitions.name: Deus Ex Savior
definitions.fullText:
Deus Ex Savior
Paladin Utility 22
You are an instrument of divine intervention, sent to save people in
their moment of dire need at the nick of time
.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You are not in line of sight of anyone who could
see you last turn and you are not in combat.
Effect: You are removed from play as you begin a journey to an
ally. At any point, in response to an immediately dangerous
situation happening to a PC, or allied NPC of narrative
importance, you may immediately appear in an empty
square adjacent to them. They can be literally anywhere,
including on a different plane. You and the DM then fill in
how you got there retroavtively, using all of your character's
resources, allies, and of course divine intervention and luck.
Once you appear, your immediate action is not u sed, and if
initiative has been rolled, yours automatically becomes right
before the creature you are saving.
(Examples of possible dangerous situations include
interrupting an attack by a trap or hazard, appearing at the
bottom of a pit to catch them, or appearing next to them as they
surrounded by guards and initiative is rolled.)
DM Notes on Deus Ex Savior:
Sometimes there’s no realistic way to appear adjacent
(the ally is surrounded by 100 guards in a small locked
room deep underground, where they can’t dramatically
fall from the sky or ceiling, for example). In which case,
the DM may either prevent the paladin from appearing
at that moment and say the player has to continue
saving that moment, or the DM can have some mercy
and allow them to appear in the scene not adjacent to
the creature they are saving. They could appear over the
horizon, or from behind a nearby tree, for example.
Player Notes: Filling in Deus Ex Savior
Retroactively With Creative:
At this level, you should have the resources to appear
almost anywhere. Even if the party has split up and you
are on literally different planes, your paladin may know
someone to help teleport them over. And if they don’t,
with the power of divine luck they happen to mee
t
someone with the skills to bring them over, or
even their
deity may intervene directly.
For example, if a sneaking rogue caught in an enemy
castle, you could say the paladin was sneaking through
and happened to succeed all those Stealth checks to
arrive next to the rogue just in time, even though they’re
usually not sneaky. Remember, much is possible when
your deity is bending the arc of history towards justice.

definitions.name: Divinely Empowered Mount
definitions.fullText:
Divinely Empowered Mount
Paladin Utility 22
A bright light surrounds your mount, and when it fades it has
undergone changes making it fit for a true champion of your deity
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine , Travel
Standard Action
Melee Touch
Target: One mount you control.
Effect: The target gains one of the following traits until your
next extended rest:
+
It gains wings, an overland fly speed equal to double
their default speed. It takes a minor action to start
flying.
+
It gains fins, and a swimming speed equal to their
default speed + 1.
+
It becomes a vessel to move between planes. They
can use the Plane Shift ritual on themselves once
per extended rest.
+
It gains magical armor and a protective aura. Their
defenses increase by +2.
+
It gains a magical chariot to pull that can carry up to
6 additional creatures.
+
It gains a hardened surface that can be used as a
weapon (a horn, enhanced antlers, empowered
horseshoes, etc). Once per encounter, it can make a
charge attack that deals an extra 1d10 damage. In
addition, they can make a charge attack against an
object or obstacle to destroy it with a +20 bonus to
Strength checks once per encounter.

definitions.name: Divine Refreshment
definitions.fullText:
Divine Refreshment
Paladin Utility 22
At the fickle whims of your deity, at your most exhausted point, yo
are energized with the will to fight. But the more you sacrifice, the
greatre your chance for reward.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine, Rest
No Action
Personal
Prerequisite : You have the Lay on Hands ability
Trigger: You spend your last healing surge with your Lay on
Hands ability; or after a short rest where you were damaged
in the last encounter protecting someone.
Effect: Roll 1d4 - 2. Gain 1 healing surge equal to the result (if
it was above 0).
If you were bloodied in your most recent encounter, you gain
an extra 1 healing surge.
If you were sent to 0 hit points your most recent encounter,
you gain an extra 1 healing surge.

Paladin Utility 22
You say a quick prayer to your deities so you can bring a swift end
to their enemies. Then, a golden light carries you towards them, a
rallies your allies to you.
Daily + Non-Combat, Divine, Ritual, Teleportation, Healing,
Travel
Standard Action
Close Burst 10
Target: Each ally in the burst (centered from the square you
started in).
Cast Time : 5 minutes.
Effect: Teleport up to 200 squares (1000 feet) towards the
location of enemies. Gain 10 + your Charisma modifier
temporary hit points. Then , teleport each target to a square
adjacent to you, or adjacent to another target you have
already teleported with this powe r. Each target also gains 10
+ your Charisma modifier temporary hit points.

had water breathing during this time, resetting the time you
can hold your breath.

Endurance of the Wolf
Ranger Utility 2
You have built up your constitution running with your beast
companion through the woods and fields
.
Daily + Non-Combat, Beast, Exploration, Travel
Standard Action
Personal
Prerequisite : You must have a wolf or stag/deer beast
companion.

a +2 bonus to Endurance checks.
This bonus is increased to a +4 bonus and you also gain a
+2 bonus to Nature, Perception, and Stealth checks if
following or tracking a creature at least a mile through
overland exploration travel or in a skill challenge.

Favored Foe
Ranger Utility 2
You are a specialist in hunting one form of monster or foe, focusin
your considerable experience as a ranger into tracking and
eliminating them.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Martial, Gathering Information
Free Action
Personal
Speical : The first time you use this power, you may select a
type of creature to be your favored foe. You may choose
from aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons,
elementals, fey, giants, immortals, monstrosities, oozes,
plants, or undead. Alternativel y, you can select two races of
humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs, or goblins and elves). You
can only change your favored foe(s) whenever you gain a
level, or, if the DM allows it, at narratively significant
moments of the story.

knowledge check related to that type of creature
this turn.
This power can only be used once per turn.
Special: You may select this same power again even if you
have already learned it to select another type of favored
foe(s).

there, surviving only on the flora and fauna, familiar to all the

Urban

Personal

type of terrain to be your favored terrain. You may choose
from arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp,
or underground (or the Underdark). Alternatively, you may
select up to two specif ic cities, towns, or villages. You can
only change your favored terrain whenever you gain a level,
or, if the DM allows it, at narratively significant moments of
the story.

Dungoneering, Insight, History, or Perception check

water, you gain twice that amount of food or water.

have already learned it to select another type of favored
foe(s).

.

Creation
Minor Action
Personal

ground.

foraging rolls. If you succeed, instead of finding food, you find

ally until your next extended rest or in the next 24 hours

incense (for Arcana, Heal, or Religion ri tuals).

definitions.name: Harvesting Useful Monster Parts
definitions.fullText:
Harvesting Useful
Ranger Utility 2
Monster Parts
You carve up a monster to find in order to appropriate claws, teeth
fangs, scales, sinew, and more to other uses.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Wilderness, Martial Practice,
Creation
Minor Action
Melee Weapon
Target: One dead non -humanoid corpse.
Cast Time: 10 minutes
Effect: You create a single non -living, non-magical object from
the target corpse. The corpse is destroyed as a result. The
object is a single weapon, a set of 10 ammunition, or item
from "Adventuring Gear" page 222 of the Player's Handbook
that can be reasonably made from the creature's corpse
(with the DM having the final word on whether such a
chosen item is reasonable). Without proper preservation, the
object lasts only until the end of your next extended rest. It
can be integrated into the crafting of a more p ermanent, but
still non-magical, item by someone with crafting abilities, but
it costs as much as the item you want to make with a 20%
discount.
At the DM's discrention, you can also create some
other non-magical object no longer than one a Medium
creature can carry.

Ranger Utility 2
Your horse is a large target enemies find hard to avoid, but woe to
those who hit them.
Encounter + Combat, Martial, Beast
Immediate Interrupt
Personal
Prerequisite: You must have a large beast companion with the
mount keyword.
Trigger : You are hit by a ranged or melee attack while
mounted on your beast companion.

damage (rounded down) is dealt to you and half (rouned up)
is dealt to your beast companion. Until the end of your next
turn, your next martial attack deals extra damage equal to
the amount dealt to your beast companion.

Ranger Utility 2
You have learned from the patient spider or careful crocodile how
attack your enemy when they are weakest.

Free Action

advantage. Also, if you hit them with an attack this turn, they
take a -2 penalty to any saving throws or escape rolls they
make until the end of their next turn.

definitions.name: Favored Foe's Language
definitions.fullText:
Favored Foe's Language
Ranger Utility 6
Following and observing your foes have given you increased
knowledge in understanding how they communicate.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial, Gathering Information,
Social
Minor Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You have the Favored Foe power (Ranger 2).
Target: One creature that is of the type of your favored foe; or
a writing or drawing made from a creature that is of the type
of your favored foe.
Effect: Make a medium DC monster knowledge check based
on the level of the target. If you succeed, you can understand
and speak a language that the target knows until the end of
the encounter and gain a +2 bonus to your next Diplomacy,
Intimidation, Insight, or Na ture check against them. If you
targeted a piece of writing or drawing, you can understand
that, although you cannot write the language yourself from
this power. If they don't speak a language, you still gain a +2
bonus to your next Insight, Nature, and Ch arisma checks to
understand and communicate with them in other ways
(hands, body language, facial expressions, etc.) although the
communication that can be given this way is often a lot
rougher and more primitive.
If you fail the monster knowledge check, you gain a
rough understanding of the language of the target, enough to
get a simple idea of what they are saying or trying to
communicate (they are angry, they are happy, etc.) unless
they are trying to hide thei r intent; or you gain a single
concept from a piece of writing (it looks like a warning, or it
sounds welcoming, etc.) but you cannot speak or write their
language.

definitions.name: Favored Terrain's Deft Exploration
definitions.fullText:
Favored Terrain's Deft
Ranger Utility 6
Exploration
You can move through your favored terrain with ease and when
guiding your party through it, travel becomes a breeze.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Travel, Wilderness
Standard Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You have the Favored Terrain power (Ranger 2).
Target: You and each ally in the party within sight and speech
range.
Effect: Until the end of your next extended rest, predominantly
difficult terrain means your overland exploration speed is
multiplied by 0.75x (instead of 0.5x). Also, your party is not
slowed by widespread difficult terrain at all during overland
exploration.
Finally, you and your allies also gain a +2 bonus to
initiative for the first combat encounter that occurs for the
duration of this power when doing overland exploration in
your favored terrain.

definitions.name: Fetch!
definitions.fullText:
Fetch!
Ranger Utility 10
Your beast companion is an expert at the game of fetch.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Beast
Free Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You have a beast companion.
Trigger A creature catches or throws a weapon or other
object. Either the thrower, target of the throw, or a square
within line -of-effect of the throw must be within the speed
distance of your beast companion.
Effect: Your beast companion shifts to somewhere between
the triggering thrower's line of effect to the catcher, or
adjacent to the thrower or target square of the thrower. The
beast companion catches the item and holds it if possible,
otherwise they drop it in th eir square.
They can then shift up to their speed again. If they
end this action adjacent to you and are holding the item, you
may take the object from them as a free action.

definitions.name: Harvesting Rare Monster Parts
definitions.fullText:
Harvesting Rare Monster
Ranger Utility 10
Parts
You begin to carve up the monster, taking the sharpest fangs, the
hardest scales, or the most pliable sinew to help you with your
journey.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Wilderness, Martial Practice,
Creation
Standard Action
Melee Weapon
Cast Time: 10 minutes.
Target: One dead non -humanoid and non -animate creature
corpse.
Effect: You create a single object from the target corpse. The
corpse is destroyed as a result. The object is a single weapon,
a set of 10 ammunition, armor, shield, a
consumable/combustible item, or other equipment that can
be reasonably made from the creature's corpse (the DM has
the final word on this). It can be magical, but generally it's
just an enhanced version of a mundane item with an
enhancement bonus depending on the level the target was
when alive, rather than containing a specific magical
enchantment.
Without proper preservation, the object lasts only
until the end of your next extended rest. It can be made into
a permanent item by someone with crafting abilities. Doing
so costs as much as the item you are trying to make with a
10% discount. It can't b e disenchanted until it's been made
into a permanent item.
You can also integrate it into the crafting of another
magic item. Doing so either gives the crafter a 10% discount
on that magic item, or at the DM's discretion they may
choose to allow the crafted item to gain a new property
based on the monster it was h arvested from instead (or in
addition to the discount). This is usually only the case for
particularly interesting parts craft from particularly rare or
interesting monsters.

definitions.name: Near-Miss Intimidating Arrow
definitions.fullText:
Near-Miss Intimidating
Ranger Utility 10
Arrow
You quicken the negotiations by demonstrating your skills,
purposefully almost hitting an enemy with an arrow.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial, Exploration, Wildernes,
Travel
Standard Action
Ranged Weapon
Requirement : You must be wielding a bow, crossbow, or
thrown weapon.
Target One creature.
Attack: Dexterity vs AC. If you are not in combat, gain a +5
bonus.
Hit: Deal no damage, but the next Intimidation check made by
you or an ally against the target gets a +5 bonus until the end
of your next turn. If you hit the enemy's AC exactly or made a
critical hit, the bonus increases to a +10 insead.
Miss: Deal 1[W] damage. If this unexpectedly initiates combat,
you and all non -Rogue allies get a -4 penalty to your initiative
roll, or the combat begins with a surprise round that everyone
but you is in. The DM may choose.
Automatic Miss: If you roll a natural 1 on the attack roll or
another form of an automatic miss , deal 3[W] damage instead.
If this initiates combat, all allies of the target get a +2 bonus to
their initiative and attack rolls the first round, in addition to
the effects of a miss from this power.

definitions.name: Speak With Other Beast s
definitions.fullText:
Speak With Other Beast s
Ranger Utility 10
Your beast companion can talk with other animals. It doesn't
necessarily mean you can understand them or the animal they're
talking to, but the beast companion may still take the initiative to
useful information, lead you somewhere useful, or get help
from the
other animals during thsi time, depending on how smart they are,
course.
Daily + Non-Combat, Primal, Beast, Social, Wilderness
Minor Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You have a beast companion. .
Effect: Until the end of the encounter, your beast companion
can speak to animal life (including beasts and magical
beasts). Animals can communicate what they have seen,
heard, or otherwise sensed within the last hour, and a hostile
animal may even try to mislead your beast companion. Your
beast companion gets a +2 bonus to Nature, Diplomacy, and
Intimidation checks with other animals during this time. This
bonus increases to a +5 bonus if they are speaking to
someone of the same species or very similar (for exampl e, an
alligator companion talking to a crocodile, a tiger companion
talking to a lion, or an eagle companion talking to a hawk or
falcon).

It doesn't necessarily mean you can understand them or the animal they're talking to, but the beast companion may still take the initiative to useful information, lead you somewhere useful, or get help from the other animals during thsi time, depending on how smart they are, course.

definitions.name: Speedy Gallop
definitions.fullText:
Speedy Gallop
Ranger Utility 10
You drive your mount to extreme speeds over hill and far away.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Beast, Travel
Minor Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be mounted.
Effect: The overland speed of your mount is increased by 3
times. This power lasts for 10 hours or until you roll initiative
for a combat encounter. You can't take actions other than
free or move actions during this time, and you can't move
silently.
Common Mount Speeds with “Speedy
Gallop”
This is about 120 miles per day for your average war
horse, 150 miles per day for your average riding horse,
this is about 75 miles per day for your average cart or
wagon.

definitions.name: Animal Pickpocket
definitions.fullText:
Animal Pickpocket
Ranger Utility 16
You and your beast companion are partners in crime, able to pilife
from unaware enemies.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial, Beast
Free Action
Personal
Prerequisite : You must have a medium or smaller beast
companion.
Requirement You and your target must not be in combat; and
the target is not aware of your beast companion.
Effect: Your beast companion can move up to its speed +4, or
move at half speed while hidden and make a Stealth check
to stay hidden. Then, the beast companion attempts a
Thievery check to pick a target's pocket or take an object the
target is holding. They either use their Thievery skill with a
+2 bonus or your Thievery skill, whichever is higher.
Afterwards, they may attempt to move half their
speed and hide with a Stealth check, or they can move up to
their speed +4 again.
If you are interacting with the target, you may make
an Easy DC Bluff check (based on the target's level) with a +2
bonus. If you succeed, the Thievery and Stealth checks get an
additional +3 bonus.
Player Notes: Animal Pickpocket
See normal rules on Thievery to Pick Pocket to see the
required DC’s and consquences for pickpocketing.

definitions.name: Harvesting for Venomous Monster Parts
definitions.fullText:
Harvesting for Venomous
Ranger Utility 1 6
Monster Parts
You begin to carve up the monster, utilizing venom sacs, poisonou
spines, acidic slime, fire bladders, and other dangerous parts of th
monster to craft dangerous poisons and oils.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Wilderness, Martial Practice,
Creation
Standard Action
Melee Weapon
Cast Time: 1 hour
Target: One dead non -humanoid, non-animate creature
corpse that had a disease, poison, acid, fire, cold, or necrotic
attack.
Effect: Roll a monster knowledge check against a moderate
DC of the target's level with a bonus equal to the highest of
your Dexterity or Strength modifier. Based on the result,
instead of gaining knowledge, you gain a poison from the
table below. It lasts only until the end of your next extended
rest. You must m eet or beast the DC from the table below in
order to create that poison. The monster's corpse cannot be
raised from the dead after you harvest it for parts in this way.
If the poison would deal damage, it deals
damage of one of the required types of damage the target
must have that they did have.
While these don't normally end to saving throws, if
the victim takes something that grants them a saving throw
to poison effects specifically, they may attempt to end the
effects of these poisons with that effect.
Monster
Result
Level
1
You hurt or poison yourself. Lose 1 healing
surge. If you cannot, take 3d6 + 10 damage.
15
You find nothing.
20
You generate a poison that can be added to
a melee or thrown weapon. It must be
applied during a short or extended rest. The
next time an attack with that weapon or
ammunition succeeds, that creature grants
combat advantage until the end of turn.
25
You generate a poison that when
consumed with food or drink causes toxic
shock and mild paralysis. It can be tasted
immediately. Roll 1d6 + 1. The poison lasts
for that times 10 minutes. Every 10
minutes until the effect ends, they roll a
medium DC Enduran ce check based on the
monster's level. If they succeed, they take
4d10 damage (for type, see the text above),
but the effect ends early. If they fail, they
take 2d10 damage, are knocked prone, and
are slowed for the next 10 minutes. If the
effect lasts until it's full duration, they take
4d10 damage at the end. Dilutes in
anything bigger than a meal or water
container for one person.
30
You generate an especially potent poison
that can be applied to a melee weapon,
thrown weapon, or a single piece of
ammunition; or can be consumed via food
or drink. The next time that weapon
successfully attacks and damages a
creature, or a creature imbibes the poison,
they lose immunity and resistance to
poison and disease effects and the chosen
damage type that the target creature dealt
(see the text above) until the end of their
next turn. If the poison was imbibed in food
or drink, it lasts for 24 hour s instead.
Dilutes in anything bigger than a meal or
water container for one person.
35
You gain a unique effect based on a power
the creature had. This extra power or effect
disappears once it is used and it only lasts
until your next short rest. I will include
some sample effects in an appendix.

definitions.name: My Ranger Needs Me
definitions.fullText:
My Ranger Needs Me
Ranger Utility 1 6
Your beast companion will escape any enclosure to reach you in
time.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Beast, Destruction
Standard Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You have a medium or larger beast companion..
Effect: Your beast companion knows you need help, no matter
their location, and they are compelled to try to travel to your
location. For the next 5 minutes or until they reach your
location, your beast companion gains a +5 bonus to Athletics
checks to jump, climb , or run. They also gain a +5 bonus to
Strength checks to break an object they are kept in (like a
stable stall, a pen, a cage, etc) and they deal double damage
to wall or door-like objects blocking the path beetween your
animal companion and you. Their ba se movement speed is
doubled. Add a +5 bonus to all their defenses until they
reach you.
They may also make a DC 20 Endurance
check in order to extend these bonuses an extra hour,
although they still end once the beast companion reaches
you.

definitions.name: Predator’s Skillful Pursuit
definitions.fullText:
Predator’s Skillful Pursuit
Ranger Utility 16
When you have a target in mind, you don't even have to actively
track them to keep aware of all signs of their passing.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial
Minor Action
Personal
Prerequisite: Trained in Athletics and/or Acrobatics.
Effect: Gain a +5 bonus to Athletics and/or Acrobatics skill
checks, whichever you're trained in, during skill checks or
skill challenges related to chases, hunting, or tracking as long
as you are the pursuer. This effect lasts for the next 5
minutes or until the end of the encounter.

definitions.name: Still Target
definitions.fullText:
Still Target
Ranger Utility 16
While there's always some challenge hitting a moving target, whe
it comes to a still target, you hit the bullseye every, single time.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Martial,, W eapon
Standard Action
Ranged Weapon
Requirement: You must be wielding a bow or crossbow.
Target: One object that isn't on someone, held by someone, or
moving.
Attack: Dexterity + 10 vs AC. This attack cannot automatically
miss and your weapon ranges are doubled. It also ignores
cover, superior cover, and concealment.
Hit: You may choose to interact with the object instead of
damaging it.
Effect: You may also gain a +10 bonus to your next
performance-related skill and ability checks when exhibiting
marksmanship against a non -moving target.

definitions.name: Subconscious Tracking
definitions.fullText:
Subconscious Tracking
Ranger Utility 16
When you have a target in mind, you don't even have to actively
track them to keep aware of all signs of their passing.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial , Travel, Gathering
Information
Standard Action
Personal
Effect: Until the end of your next extended rest or combat
encounter, your passive Perception gets a +5 bonus for the
purpose of knowing if you pass a sign of someone or
something you are tracking.
During this time, if you are tracking a group and
succeed a Medium DC active check (based on the creature
with the lowest level of the group), you also know how many
are in the area, their sizes, and how long ago they they
passed the immediate area.
During this time if you roll initiative to fight a target
you've been tracking, you get a +2 bonus to your initiative.
Favored Foe: If you have the Favored Foe power (Ranger 2),
the Passive Perception bonus increases to a +10 bonus and
the initiative bonus increases to a +5 bonus when related to
your favored foe.

track them to keep aware of all signs of their passing.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial , Travel, Wilderness
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement : You must be exploring or traveling in the
wilderness, outside of an urban settlement.
Effect: Choose one bonus from the list below. The bonuses last
until your next short or extended rest, until initiative is rolled
for combat, or you arrive in a town, village, or other urban
settlement of some sort. If combat is only one round or
completed with th e Quick and Dirty Fighting rules, it does
not interrupt this effect.
+
Gain a +5 bonus to your next Nature or
Dungeoneering check to not become lost or to
navigate a route, as long as you have been to this
place before, planned a route previously through a
map or directions, or have a map now.
+
You can navigate stealthily while traveling at a
normal pace. In addition, you gain a +2 bonus to
Stealth checks while traveling through the wild or
over long distances.
+
You can maintain alertness while doing another
activity when doing overland travel/exploration.
You can also scout and do another job during this
time, and you gain a +2 bonus to your Perception
checks while traveling through the wild or over long
distances..
Favored Terrain : If you have the Favored Terrain (Ranger 2)
power, the first bonus from the list above increases to a +10
when on your favored terrain, and the second and third
bonuses from the list above increase to a +5.

definitions.name: Beast Companion of Great Renown
definitions.fullText:
Beast Companion of
Ranger Utility 22
Great Renown
Your beast companion is a legend in their own right, appearing on
banners and coat-of-arms, spreading both fear and a rallying point
when appearing on the battlefield.
Daily + Non-Combat, Beast, Renown, War
Standard Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You must have a medium or large beast
companion..
Effect: Until the end of your next extended rest or until your
beast companion dies, all allies get a +2 power bonus to
their Intimidation checks against enemies to cause fear or
their Diplomacy checks to inspire, as long as the targets can
see or hear your beast companion and they are within 10
squares of your beast companion.
Renown: If you are using Renown rules, while under the
effects of this power, your influence bonus from renown
increases from a +2 to a +4.
Warfare: If you are using Warfare rules, if you are in a warfare
encounter, choose an allied unit. That unit gains a +4 influence
bonus to Morale and Command checks if your beast
companion is alive. The effects of this power end at the end of
that encounter.

definitions.name: Carving the Terrain
definitions.fullText:
Carving the Terrain
Ranger Utility 22
You concentrate for a moment on the terrain ahead of you, then r
across the battlefield in a blink of an eye, using your blades to cut
and shape the ground, trees, stone, and area in general to be mor
you and your allies' favor.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Wilderness, Weapon,
Destruction
Standard Action
Close Burst 20
Requirement : You must be wielding two melee weapons .
Effect: You may change the shape of the blast into a rectangle
of an equal number or lesser number of squares. It can't be
more than 100 squares on a side. Until the end of your next
turn, you may spend a move and a standard action to choose
a number of squares equal to 1 + Dexterity modifier +
Strength modifier, doubled. You may choose the same
squares multiple times. For each square chosen, you may
choose one of the following effects below to apply in it.
Afterwards, you may teleport yourself to any empty square
within but on the far side of the blast.
+
If the square has difficult terrain caused by an object,
you may remove it. It is destroyed or moved to
another square in the area of effect.
+
You may place difficult terrain in a square (such as
by cutting up the ground or cutting an object and
leaving debris there).
+
You may remove an object causing a blocking
obstacle ot terrain and reduce it to only causing
difficult terrain.
+
You may make an attack or Strength check against
an object in that square.
+
You may attack a creature in that square. If you are
in combat, this attack has a -5 penalty unless the
creature is helpless.

definitions.name: Delayed Falling Arrow
definitions.fullText:
Delayed Falling Arrow
Ranger Utility 22
You shoot an arrow into the sky with perfect predictive clarity. It h
a long fall down, making it easy to dodge but also making it easy t
hit or fall into objects, and making it difficult to tell who and where
came from.
Daily + Non-Combat, Martial, Wilderness, Weapon
Standard Action
Ranged 1 mile (varies, see below)
Requirement: You must be wielding a bow or crossbow. You
must also be able to shoot straight up into the sky, such as
when in the outdoors or in an outdoors -like area.
Effect: You shoot an arrow into the sky, beyond seeing
distance. At any point in the next hour, as long as you are still
within a mile of where you shot the arrow and still outdoors,
you may have the arrow from an origin point somewhere in
the sky to any square ne ar you that you choose. It does not
have to be within line -of-sight, nor within line -of-sight or line-
of-effect of the original shot.
If you choose to have it fall into a square with a
creature, you may have it apply a basic ranged attack to the
creature but it gets a -5 penalty. The attack does not seem to
originate from you, and you can choose to have it appear to
come from someone els e with a successful Bluff + 3 check vs
passive Insight made by you or an ally.
DM Notes: If the story takes place over wider distances, the
DM is encouraged to increase the maximum distance of this
power an extra 1, 2, or even 3 miles. If they want, they can
use the excuse of an exceptionally clear day, low wind, or
you are just that good.
