definitions.name: Gather Your Swarm
definitions.fullText:
Gather Your Swarm
Ranger Utility 22
You send out your beast companion to gather a swarm of its own
type to do your bidding, accomplishing non
-violent, but otherwise
helpful tasks.
Daily + Non-Combat, Beast, Wilderness, Binding
Standard Action
Ranged 20
Prerequisite : You must have a small or tiny beast companion.
Effect: You summon a swarm of creatures that are of a similar
type to your beast companion and local to the area (if they
exist) in an empty square within range. If you are in an area
where your beast companion is local or a similar creature is,
it will appear at the end of your next turn, otherwise, it may
sometimes take up to an hour if it's possible at all.
The swarm has similar stats as your beast
companion, including the same keywords, movement
abilities, skill bonuses, ability scores, resistances,
vulnerabilities, senses, etc. However, it has triple the the
health pool, a +4 to its Fortitude and Will defen ses, has
resistance half damage to melee and ranged attacks, and
vulnerability double damage from area and burst attacks. It
takes up an area 2 times larger than the original creature, but
can squeeze in any space one creature of the swarm can fit
into. It also has a -10 penalty to Stealth checks.
You can direct the swarm to do straightforward,
simple tasks through giving directions to your animal
companion. It will not attempt to interfere in combat, and will
run away from situations it perceives as dangerous. It will stick
around for 1 hour if not given a task or given a few short term
tasks. If it is given a longer term task, it will stick around up to
the end of your next extended rest to see it completed. If your
beast companion is killed or knocked unconscious, the swarm
will dissipate and leav e.

definitions.name: Charming Rapscallion
definitions.fullText:
Charming Rapscallion
Rogue Utility 2
You've charmed your way past more marks than you can count,
turning wary strangers into fast friends with little more than a
grin and a good story.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Social, Deception
Minor Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You must have training in Diplomacy or Bluff.
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, gain a +1 bonus to
your next Bluff or Diplomacy check to persuade, sell
something, or increase the impression or favorability
someone has of you. If this is the first time you've met this
NPC ever, the bonus increases to a +3. If you have ever
done a negative action against this creature (tricked,
swindled, cheated, stolen from, attacked, etc) and they
recognize you, then you cannot use this power on them.

You stand behind someone, making them feel surrounded and
more scared.

you want to intimidate, and an ally of yours who is also
trying to intimidate them is in front of them, both you and
that ally get a +2 bonus to their Intimidation check
instead.

definitions.name: Stance of the Bone Crushing Thug
definitions.fullText:
Stance of the Bone
Rogue Utility 2
Crushing Thug
You sacrifice speed for the terrifying gait of a ruthless killer,
sizing up your enemy's weakest bones and veins as you approac
them.
Daily + Combat, Martial, Stance
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: While in this stance, your speed is reduced by 1. But,
you deal an extra die of sneak attack damage when
wielding a club or mace. In addition, when a weapon
attack you make with a club or mace deals damage to a
rattled enemy, it deals extra damage equal t o your
Strength modifier. You may leave and enter this stance
until the end of this encounter with a minor action.

definitions.name: Cunning Advice
definitions.fullText:
Cunning Advice
Rogue Utility 6
You are able to aid allies from afar just by giving good advice or
good plan of action.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Social
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be trained in a skill.
Target: One ally that can hear you, understands your
language, and is within line of sight.
Effect: Roll an Aid Another check to aid the target ally with
a skill you are trained in, against a DC of 10 + half the
level of the creature you are aiding + 2. If you succeed,
they gain a +2 bonus to their next check with that same
skill until the end of the en counter. Cunning Sneak: You
may add your Intelligence modifier as the bonus instead of
the +2.

definitions.fullText:
Cunning Improvisation
Rogue Utility 6
A loose flagstone, a swinging blade, a patch of oil
—you see not a
hazard but an opportunity waiting to be pointed the right way.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Combat, Exploration
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: Choose a trap, hazard, or terrain power in the area. If
the chosen trap, hazard, or terrain power can’t affect
enemies, you become aware of this and you regain the use
of this power. Otherwise, until your next short or extended
rest, the next time that trap, hazard, or terrain power
would target a creature, it gains a +2 bonus or takes a -2
penalty to its attack roll (your choice). If it hits, you may
have it deal extra damage equal to your Sneak Attack.

Charisma modifier. Cunning Sneak: You may increase the
attack bonus and the damage dealt by your Intelligence
modifier.

I Know a Guy Who
Rogue Utility 6
Knows a Guy
You may not know how to do the thing, but you know someone
who does. “Translating an ancient text? No idea. But a professo
at the local university probably could, and I know how to get
there.”

Standard Action
Personal
Effect: Make a Streetwise check with a +3 bonus to find a
type of person who can get you a piece of information. If
you succeed, you also learn their general or usual location
and how to get there.

and how to get there.

ruleFields.text: Make a Streetwise check with a +3 bonus to find a type of person who can get you a piece of information. If you succeed, you also learn their general or usual location and how to get there.

definitions.name: Modify Item Quality Appearance
definitions.fullText:
Modify Item Quality
Rogue Utility 6
Appearance
You make something look more decrepit, new, or mundane than
it actually is.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Deception, Restoration
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be wielding a Disguise Kit, a
Forgery Kit, or a kit relevant to the item you are modifying
(such as Blacksmith’s Tools if modifying a weapon or
armor, or Carpenter’s Tools if modifying something
wooden).
Effect: Choose one of the following effects:
New: Make the target object seem new and
unblemished, masking any flaws, age, breakage, or
imperfections. Using a broken object for its purpose
reveals its true state. Creatures familiar with that type of
object can attempt a saving throw when they first inter act
with the object to overcome the disguise, and every hour
thereafter that they continue to interact with it.
Decrepit: Make the target object seem like a
worthless, aged, useless, rusting, or otherwise decrepit
version of itself. Using an object that seems broken for its
purpose reveals its true state. Creatures familiar with that
type of object can attempt a saving throw when they first
interact with the object to overcome the disguise, and
every hour thereafter that they continue to interact with it.
Mundane: Make an object that is especially
interesting or blemished appear like a mundane,
unremarkable version of itself; a magical longsword seems
ordinary, a broken spear looks like every other on the rack,
a long-unused throne seems standard. Interacting with the
object directly reveals its true state immediately if it is
magical; otherwise the user gets a saving throw to discover
the disguise.

definitions.name: Must Have Been the Wind
definitions.fullText:
Must Have Been the
Rogue Utility 6
Wind
You mess up and make a sound, but on their way to check on yo
others simply find a cat, a window someone must have left open
or something else innocuous.
Daily + Non-Combat, Deception, Exploration
Immediate Reaction
Personal
Requirement: You are out of combat.
Trigger: You fail a Stealth check against creatures that are
not aware of you, can’t see you, and whose line of sight
you are not within.
Effect: You may reroll the Stealth check. You must use the
second result. If the roll succeeds in hiding you, you may
then immediately move up to your speed + 2 to another
location that you can hide behind or in. You are hidden
during and after this move.

definitions.name: Nothing Up My Sleeve
definitions.fullText:
Nothing Up My Sleeve
Rogue Utility 6
A knife is only as good as your ability to have it when they
thought they took everything.
Daily (Special) + Non-Combat, Deception, Martial
Practice
Standard Action
Personal
Effect: You hide any number of weapons on your person so
that they cannot be found. Make a Thievery check with a
+10 bonus. The next time you are searched for one of the
following weapons, the searcher must beat a Perception
check equal to your Thievery check res ult to find it. The
weapons must be small, one -handed, and one of the
following categories: dagger, shuriken, or sling (but not its
ammunition).
Special: You can use this power twice before each extended
rest. Whenever it is used a second time after an extended
rest, you may choose to keep the Thievery check result
you got the first time instead of rolling again.

definitions.name: Ranged Distraction
definitions.fullText:
Ranged Distraction
Rogue Utility 6
A pebble skips off a far wall, a crate rattles in the dark
—every eye
snaps the wrong way, and that’s all you need.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Deception, Exploration
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be wielding a crossbow, sling, or
thrown weapon.
Effect: Choose a square within range of your weapon.
Nearby creatures that you are hidden from hear a noise or
disturbance coming from that square. If enemies choose to
face that area, this counts as enough of a distraction to
enable you and allies who are behind those enemies to
make a Stealth check even if they are not behind full cover
or total concealment (as per the distraction part of the
Stealth rules). Enemies close enough to hear the noise take
a -2 penalty to Perception checks to perceive other
creatures until they move to that square or see you or an
ally trying to hide.

definitions.name: Secret Speech (Rogue)
definitions.fullText:
Secret Speech (Rogue)
Rogue Utility 6
With pre-established codewords, you and your crew are able to
have an entirely different conversation than the one the people
around you hear.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Deception, Social
Standard Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You must be trained in Bluff.
Effect: Until the end of the encounter, you can send secret
messages embedded in normal speech to allies in the
nearby area who can hear you and understand your
language. You must have had at least one long rest with
an ally for them to understand you. Delivering a secret
message generally takes twice as long as the message
would otherwise take to relay. If an enemy becomes
aware you are sending secret messages in your normal
speech, they can try to figure it out with an Insight check
vs. DC 10 + your current bonu s to Bluff checks.

definitions.name: Threats Come True
definitions.fullText:
Threats Come True
Rogue Utility 6
Like a proper thug, you are not only good at making threats, bu
you are good at realizing them.
Daily + Non-Combat, Social
No Action
Personal
Requirement: You are not in combat.
Trigger: You succeeded on an Intimidate check against a
creature or group of creatures you’ve been talking to for at
least 1 minute.
Effect: If you roll initiative to enter a combat encounter
against any of the triggering creatures before your next
extended rest, all of the triggering creatures that are in
that encounter as an enemy are rattled until the end of
their first turn. Ruthless Ruffian: Targeted enemies also
take a -2 penalty to their initiative check.

Underworld Contact
Rogue Utility 6
Everyone you ever ran with left a door cracked open somewhere
You still know which ones to knock on.
Daily + Non-Combat, Gathering Information, Urban,
Social
Standard Action
Personal
Effect: Make a Streetwise check with a bonus equal to the
higher of your Intelligence modifier or +2 to reach out to
an old contact in the area. Depending on the result, you
find them if able, or you easily learn whether they’ve
moved on from the area. A result b elow 10 means you
can’t find or access them this time. When you use this
power, determine whether you are asking for a favor or for
knowledge; it must relate to their purview.
Favor: A favor may require persuasion depending
on your past. Diplomacy and similar social rolls to
convince them gain a modifier based on the Social Mod of
the check result (in addition to DM modifiers for the
favor’s nature and size). You may raise their Influ ence /
Access one row, but the Social Mod worsens by a further -
2 (you did not part on good terms). The DM may let this
improve during play by doing favors for the NPC.
Knowledge: Roll a knowledge check using your
own stats to see if the contact can answer your question; if
they can, gain a bonus to your next knowledge check
while talking to them, as long as it is information they
would reasonably know (often set by the Influence /
Access column).

definitions.name: Artful Wound
definitions.fullText:
Artful Wound
Rogue Utility 10
You impress or terrify by throwing with such accuracy as to
purposefully graze your target.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Social, Weapon
Standard Action
Ranged Weapon
Requirement: You must be wielding a crossbow or thrown
weapon (light blade, axe, or spear only).
Target: One creature.
Attack: Dexterity vs AC
Hit: Deal 1 damage, but the next Intimidate check made by
you against the target or its watching allies gains a +5
bonus until the end of your next turn. You can instead
choose to grant that bonus to a Diplomacy or similar
check, as part of a performance to am aze or impress the
target or a watching audience. This damage cannot reduce
the target to 0 or fewer hit points.
Miss: Deal 1[W] damage. If this unexpectedly initiates
combat, you take a -2 penalty to your attack rolls during the
first round.

definitions.name: Equipment Review
definitions.fullText:
Equipment Review
Rogue Utility 10
A professional doesn’t blame their tools, but they know they are
only as good as them. You take the time during a break to revie
clean, organize, and improve your tools.
Daily + Non-Combat, Rest, Restoration
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be taking a short or extended rest.
Effect: Choose an equipment or tool kit that you or an ally
resting with you has. If it grants any equipment bonuses to
skills, it grants an additional +2 bonus to those skill checks
with that tool until your next short or extended rest.

definitions.name: Making a Plan
definitions.fullText:
Making a Plan
Rogue Utility 10
You sit your crew down to mastermind a plan for them, crafting
a plan that if executed exactly as you say can hardly fail.
Daily + Non-Combat, Rest, Social, Exploration, Physical
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be taking a short or extended rest.
Target: You and any number of allies resting with you who
are not currently using another rest ability.
Effect: For each target, choose a skill or ability check and a
specific activity or use for that check, then give that target
a d4 Plan die. Until the end of your next extended rest, the
target can roll the Plan die and add both it and your
Intelligence modifier to any check they make that matches
the skill or ability and the specific use you chose for them,
or to an Aid Another check when helping another
character make that same check for that same use.

and balancing or squeezing, Stealth and moving quietly or
hiding, Thievery and picking locks or pickpocketing, Bluff
and lying or Bluff and disguise.

a d4 Plan die. Until the end of your next extended rest, the
target can roll the Plan die and add both it and your

the skill or ability and the specific use you chose for them,
or to an Aid Another check when helping another
character make that same check for that same use.

You turn the weapon over in your hands where they can see it,
and let them imagine the rest. They know what you can do with
it. Or they will soon.

Standard Action
Personal

to your next Intimidate check if you have a light blade,
club, or mace. If your weapon counts as both a light blade
and a mace, the bonus increases to +4 instead. Combat: If
you successfully attack an o pponent with a light blade,
club, or mace you are wielding with a weapon attack, this
power can be used as an immediate reaction that turn and
the bonus increases to +5. Ruthless Ruffian: If that attack
used a club or mace, it also deals 5 extra damage.

definitions.name: Sabotage Trap
definitions.fullText:
Sabotage Trap
Rogue Utility 10
A few simple modifications is all it takes to cause an enemy to
stumble into the same trap they set up. “Something has change
they think, as they hear the familiar click before the blade come
swinging down.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Exploration, Destruction
Standard Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You must be trained in Thievery.
Requirement: You must have a trap -making kit.
Target: One trap or hazard.
Effect: Make a Thievery check against the DC to disable the
target trap or hazard, or against a DC of your level + 10 if
it does not have one. If you succeed and the target trap or
hazard does not trigger on or target enemies, a specific
creature, or a type of creature, you change it so that it now
does, and so that it does not target you or your allies. If it is
a trap, you may also change the type of damage it deals
from one type to another. If you fail, you gain a +2 bonus
to the next skill check you make to tr y to disable that trap
or hazard.

definitions.name: Unexpected KO
definitions.fullText:
Unexpected KO
Rogue Utility 10
One clean strike behind the ear, and they simply fold. Nobody
hears a thing.
Daily + Non-Combat, Deception, Weapon
Standard Action
Melee or Ranged Weapon
Requirement: You must be wielding a club, a mace, or a
sling or thrown weapon (flail or hammer only). You cannot
be in combat.
Target: One non -Elite, non-Solo creature that is at least 3
levels below you and that is not aware of your presence.
Attack: Dexterity vs AC. If the target is a minion, this attack
automatically succeeds.
Hit: The creature is knocked unconscious. This lasts for 1
hour, until another creature wakes it with a standard
action, or until it is dealt damage. If this was a melee
attack and you were not revealed to other enemies when
using this power, you regain the us e of this power. It can
only be regained twice this way.
Level 22: At level 22, this power can last up to 8 hours for
creatures below level 10. And you can regain it up to four
times this way.

definitions.name: Dramatic Disappearance
definitions.fullText:
Dramatic Disappearance
Rogue Utility 16
“We’re going to want to enter from there,” they say, pointing a
window. “Consider it done,” they hear you reply behind them.
“But how will you…?” But when they turn around to finish the
question, you’re already gone, as if you were never there.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Deception, Exploration
Free Action
Personal
Requirement: You are out of combat.
Trigger: All non -PC creatures you are interacting with in the
area are distracted, or are turned away and not looking at
you for any reason.
Target: All triggering creatures.
Effect: Make a Stealth check with a +2 bonus against the
highest passive Perception among the creatures you are
interacting with. If you succeed, you may quietly move up
to twice your speed. You must end this movement
somewhere you can hide, at which point you
automatically become hidden from all targets. You gain a
+2 bonus to all skill checks to jump, climb, or swim during
this movement. If you cannot end this movement in a
position to hide, you are assumed not to have moved in
the first place, and you regain th e use of this power.
Although the targets do not detect you leaving, and may
even be in the middle of a sentence, you get the gist of the
rest of their thought as if you had stayed there listening to
them.

definitions.name: Evasive Parkour
definitions.fullText:
Evasive Parkour
Rogue Utility 16
Every rooftop, railing, and rain barrel is a door out. Whoever is
behind you has to take the long way.
Daily + Non-Combat, Physical, Exploration
Minor Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You must be trained in Athletics or
Acrobatics.
Effect: Gain a +5 bonus to Athletics and/or Acrobatics skill
checks, whichever you’re trained in, during skill checks or
skill challenges related to chases, hunting, or tracking as
long as you are the pursued. This effect lasts for the next 5
minutes or until the end of the encounter.

definitions.name: Impenetrable Lie
definitions.fullText:
Impenetrable Lie
Rogue Utility 16
Lying is so ingrained in you that people can’t get the truth from
you even when you are magically compelled or your mind is rea
Daily + Non-Combat, Deception, Warding
Minor Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You must be trained in Bluff.
Effect: For the next 1 hour, you cannot be compelled to
speak the truth, nor can your mind be read, by any
external effect. In addition, any bonuses to Insight checks
against you, or penalties to your Bluff checks, from powers,
items, or rituals are negated. You can choose whether the
caster of these abilities knows that it failed or still thinks
they succeeded.

definitions.name: Master of Disguise (Rogue)
definitions.fullText:
Master of Disguise
Rogue Utility 22
(Rogue)
The guards rush in. “Give up! You’re surrounded.” Suddenly, one
of the guards takes out a knife and places it on the throat of a
different. Looks like they’re not so surrounded after all.
Daily + Non-Combat, Deception
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must have a Disguise Kit on your person.
You are hidden from anyone who could see and you are
not in combat. You must also have at least 1 healing surge
and 1 action point.
Effect: Spend 1 healing surge. You are removed from play
for at least 1 hour. After that, at any point during play that
is either outside of combat or as initiative is being rolled,
you may spend 1 action point to choose a nameless filler
NPC or minion enemy (ran dom cultist #5, city guard who
comes to investigate you breaking into a house, shop
keep’s assistant, etc.) in the scene and reveal that they are
actually you in disguise.
You can remain in this out -of-play state as long as you
choose, up to the next time initiative is rolled for a combat
encounter. If you have still not revealed yourself by that
point and there are no valid disguise targets, the DM must
introduce a valid NP C to the scene for you to reveal
yourself as by the end of the first round of combat.
Special: This can only be used once per level.
DM Note: The DM may choose to expand the things you
can disguise yourself as, such as named NPCs, non -minion
enemies, etc. In addition, replaced NPCs are often
assumed to be knocked out somewhere and may appear
again in a later encounter.

definitions.fullText:
Planning the Operation
Rogue Utility 22
You spend the downtime asking the worst question you know:
what if it all goes wrong? By the time you move, every answer is
already in your pocket.

Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be taking a short or extended rest.
Effect: You gain the secondary power Backup Plan
Flashback (Short) or Backup Plan Flashback (Extended)
respectively. You can use it at any point until your next
short or extended rest respectively, a number of times
depending on when you used this power: once for a short
rest, three times for an extended rest.
Special: If this power is used during an extended rest, you
do not regain it during your next extended rest.

definitions.name: Zephyr’s Parkour
definitions.fullText:
Zephyr’s Parkour
Rogue Utility 22
You stand still and read the route like a page
- every ledge, gap,
and handhold, in order. Then you simply go, and nothing
between here and there gets a vote.
Daily + Non-Combat, Physical, Exploration
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You are out of combat.
Effect: Choose a spot within line of sight and within 4 times
your speed. You take one full turn to breathe, focus, and
identify your route. Next turn, you may use a move action
to move to the spot you chose, and are assumed to
succeed on every check required to reach that spot
(examples: climbing, jumping, balancing, etc.). If it is
impossible to reach that square even with rolling 20s on
all your checks, you gain that knowledge and regain the
use of this power, but the action is still expended.

If more than one target is spotted while you are in this stance, it ends.

definitions.name: Bird Calls
definitions.fullText:
Bird Calls
Warlord Utility 2
A whistle here, a warble there
— a private language hidden in the
ordinary sounds of the wild.
Daily + Non -Combat, Wilderness, Rest
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must currently be taking a short or
extended rest in an area with local wildlife that makes
sounds.
Effect: You establish a set of signals that you and any allies
resting with you understand. Choose up to 10 different
signals and the message or phrase they are trying to
communicate. They sound exactly like the local wildlife.
You can make such sounds without mak ing a check, and
they can be heard up to 1000 feet away. After hearing it,
an ally can make a Medium DC Nature or Perception
check to determine your general distance away and
direction. Your allies that were resting with you when you
used this power must m ake a Nature check based on your
level - Easy if the area has a lot of low level wildlife, or a
Medium Nature check if it has barely any or only high level
wildlife - in order to gain access to the same calls. You and
your allies can use these calls to mak e these signals until
the next time you use this power, although they are only
useful while near the current environment.
Per the DM's prerogative, dense, forested areas, noisy wind,
or other similar areas that can shorten sound may shorten
the distance it can be heard up to half. Optimal conditions,
such as an open area with soft wind to carry sound, or an
echoing space, may increase the distance the calls can be
heard up to 1 mile.
Bird Call Signal Examples
Some example signals you and your allies might
establish: “Danger”, “Help!”, “Come back quick!”,
“Run away!”, “All clear”, “Enemy spotted, move
in”, “Enemy spotted, hide.”

Warlord Utility 2
Distraction
A good officer never lets a slip become a disaster
— you draw the
enemy's attention onto yourself so your people can melt back in
the dark.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Exploration, Deception
Immediate
Personal
Reaction
Trigger: You or an ally fails a Stealth check.
Effect: You and all other allies that aren't the triggered
creature gain a +1 bonus to Stealth checks this turn and
until the end of your next turn. If it was part of a group
Stealth check or Skill Challenge, it's a +2 bonus instead.

definitions.name: Intimidating Stunt
definitions.fullText:

Warlord Utility 2
You stun and terrify onlookers with your risky and brave
maneuvers.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Social, Physical
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You succeed a Medium or Hard skill check that
involves Strength or Dexterity, or use such a skill check to
bypass difficult or hindering terrain, or a similar danger.
Effect: You may make an immediate Intimidation check
with a +2 bonus (even if it would normally take a standard
action).

definitions.name: Mind for Maps
definitions.fullText:
Mind for Maps
Warlord Utility 2
Every road, ridge, and old battlefield you've ever studied is filed
away in your head, ready the moment you need it.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Exploration, Travel, War
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +2 bonus
to History skill checks for military history, wars, battles,
grand strategy, etc. In addition, this bonus also applies to
skill checks related to geography or navigation (often
Nature or Dungeoneering).

definitions.fullText:
Natural Leader
Warlord Utility 2
People look to you when things fall apart
— a steady word from
you turns a frightened crowd into a functioning team.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Social
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, gain a +2 bonus to
Diplomacy skill checks when directing or giving orders to
an NPC if they are not unfriendly to you. If the target NPC
is experiencing a moment of crisis or panic, the bonus
increases to a +4.

definitions.name: Pre-Battle Rituals
definitions.fullText:
Pre-Battle Rituals
Warlord Utility 2
Before a big battle, you have your own rituals of preparation,
whether it's a quiet contemplation or a loud hyping yourself up.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Rest, Battle Preparation
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be taking a short or extended rest.
Effect: You gain temporary hit points equal to your
Charisma or Wisdom modifier until the end of the first
turn of your next combat encounter (or at the beginning of
your next short or extended rest).
Bravura: The temporary hit points instead last until the end
of your next combat encounter.

definitions.name: Running Cadence
definitions.fullText:
Running Cadence
Warlord Utility 2
You set a marching chant that keeps everyone's feet moving lon
after they'd normally drop.
Daily + Non -Combat, Travel
Standard Action
Personal
Effect: You and your allies may make a DC 20 Endurance
check to continue traveling overland at a fast pace beyond
1 hour. If you fail, you must spend a healing surge or take
damage equal to your level as normal. The DC increases
by 5 every hour after that. In addi tion, if you or an ally
would take damage from this, they take only half the
damage instead.

definitions.name: Setup Camp Quickly
definitions.fullText:
Setup Camp Quickly
Warlord Utility 2
You've spent so much camped out for war, that by the time you
buddies have taken off their armor and sat down, you have
already assembled the campsite. And you can tear it down with
equal speed.
At-Will + Non -Combat, Travel, Rest, Martial Practice
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 5 minutes (setup), 1 minute (teardown)
Effect: You can use this power to quickly setup or teardown
a campsite during the cast time. When setting one up, you
clear the area, set up tents, unroll bedrolls, create a fire if
you have a way to do so, and setup buckets and pans for
whoever gathers the water and cooks the food. When
tearing one down, you teardown and pack up the tents,
pack up the supplies, put out the fire, and clear the area as
if you were never there. You use you and your allies'
existing gear when setting up the camp.

definitions.name: Study the Battlefield
definitions.fullText:
Study the Battlefield
Warlord Utility 2
You see a barrel of Dwarven Fire Whiskey and remember the
history of the brew and the rumors of it's numerous explosive
accidents. You smile to yourself as you think that it's time for a
little fireworks.
At-Will + Non -Combat, Gathering Information, Battle
Preparation
Free Action
Personal
Effect: You get a +2 bonus to Perception checks to identify
key features of a battlefield and a bonus to skill checks to
identify what they are, except for traps. This includes
facets of the terrain, hazards, possible terrain powers,
illusions on the terrain, etc.
Study the Battlefield DM Notes
The DM can add a +2 to identify traps or aspects
of traps if someone uses this power on them and
the DM doesn’t want to give away that it’s a trap.

definitions.name: Tactical Knowledge
definitions.fullText:
Tactical Knowledge
Warlord Utility 2
You read the flow of a fight the way others read a book
— where
the line will break, who's about to flank, what the enemy wants
Encounter + Non -Combat, War
Free Action
Personal
Effect: Gain a +3 bonus to the roll of a Tactics skill if you
have it. If you do not, gain a +2 bonus to a similar skill or
ability check (often Insight or Intelligence).
Special: When you select this power, if the DM allows, you
gain a new skill called Tactics (Int) if yo su don't already
have it. It can be used to read what enemies are planning
to do next, how they fight, how an enemy squad or
military runs, spotting weaknesses in enemies or the
environment, etc. It can also be used as a monster
knowledge roll for enemy hum anoids that fight in groups.

definitions.name: Tactical Retreat
definitions.fullText:
Tactical Retreat
Warlord Utility 2
You see that there is no winning the situation and are able to
execute a more effective retreat to save your people.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: You or an ally must lose 1 healing surge. The DM
interrupts the combat encounter with a skill challenge.
The skill challenge is created with the players; together
you all decide its goal. The negative consequence for
losing is generally just resuming the combat, though often
in a different place farther away from the initial battle,
depending on how many successful checks the party got
before they failed the skill challenge.
The difficulty of the skill challenge is dependent on the
difference in level between the players and the enemies;
the DCs of the checks themselves are dependent on the
level of the highest enemy. The players escape far enough
away to take a short rest if they succeed. The DM is free to
adjust the difficulty of the skill challenge depending on
other enemy factors as well.

Advice
You improve the leadership or mentorship skills of someone else
so that you all can benefit from their wisdom together.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Social
Standard Action
Close Burst 100

language.
Effect: The target may choose an ally of theirs who can hear
them and understand their language. The next time this
encounter that the chosen ally makes an Aid Another
check to aid the target, that Aid Another check grants a
+4 bonus instead of the usual +2.

definitions.name: Catch Them!
definitions.fullText:
Catch Them!
Warlord Utility 6
You lunge to catch a comrade before the ground
— or the enemy
— can claim them.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Physical
Immediate
Ranged 5
Interrupt
Trigger: An ally is falling, or is pushed, pulled, slid, or
knocked prone.
Target: An ally within 5 squares of the triggering ally.
Effect: The target moves up to their speed to a square
adjacent to the triggering ally. If the triggering ally is
falling, they land on the targeted ally and both take half of
any falling damage. Otherwise, reduce the number of
squares they are being pushed, pulle d, or slid by 1. If they
would be knocked prone from falling or the forced
movement effect, they are not.

definitions.name: Delegate Skill Challenge
definitions.fullText:
Delegate Skill
Warlord Utility 6
Challenge
You ask an ally to take the lead during their moment of expertis
to quickly and smoothly accomplish your whole team's goals.
Daily + Non -Combat, Social, Physical
No Action
Personal
Trigger: It is your turn to take an action during a skill
challenge.
Effect: You may have an ally make an action during the skill
challenge instead. This doesn't count as their action for the
round. They get a +1 bonus to any skill checks they make
during that action.
When Delegating Matters
This power earns its keep at tables where a skill
challenge runs in rounds and every player is
expected to act before the next round begins
—
handing your action to an ally is a real concession
of the spotlight. If your skill challenges are looser,
with pl ayers contributing whenever they have an
idea, it does much less work.

Find Traps
Warlord Utility 6
“Well, I’d know that I would trap this area if I was them…”
Daily + Non -Combat, Exploration, Martial, Zone
Standard Action
Close Burst 10
Effect: You create a zone around you that follows you as you
move until the end of your next turn. You are able to
detect if a trap is within this zone and within your line of
sight, but not the exact location of it. It must be specifically
intended to cause harm by its creator (so natural hazards
don’t count). This power merely reveals that a trap is
present in the zone. You don’t learn the location of each
trap, but you do learn the general nature of the danger
posed by a trap you sense.

definitions.name: I Got a Bad Feeling About This
definitions.fullText:
I Got a Bad Feeling
Warlord Utility 6
About This
When all else fails, you know to listen to your gut.
Daily + Non -Combat, Divination
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: You can ask the DM one question about the current
situation or an action you or the party is about to take. The
DM can only respond with “You have a good feeling about
this,” “You have a bad feeling about this,” or “You have
mixed feelings about this.” If it’s the last answer, the DM
should at least give some sort of ratio of good to bad
feelings.
Special: You may use this power twice before each
extended rest.
Reading the Gut
Answer this power from what the character could
plausibly sense
— the tension in a room, the
wrongness of a too -quiet road — rather than from
what the party hasn’t discovered yet. A bad
feeling flags danger, not its source. When the
answer is mixed, a roug h ratio (“mostly good, but
something here is off”) gives the party something
to act on without handing them the plot.

You take your place at the head of the charge, where a
commander belongs.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Battle Preparation
No Action
Personal
Trigger: You roll initiative for a combat encounter and you
are not surprised.

you gain a +2 bonus to your initiative check. On the first
round of combat, you also gain a +2 bonus to your attack
rolls, skill checks, and ability checks — as long as you end
your standard action clo ser to an enemy — until the end of
your first turn.

definitions.name: Old War Buddy (Warlord)
definitions.fullText:
Old War Buddy
Warlord Utility 6
(Warlord)
You look around with recognition at this place. “Well I’ll be
— this
is where my old campaign comrade settled down. Come on, if I
know them, they’ll be at the nearest tavern trading war stories,
and they still owe me for pulling them off the line at Kellen
’s Ford.
If anyone can tell us what’s going on here, it’s them.”
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Social, Gathering
Information
Standard Action
Personal
Special: The first time you use this power you may
designate a nearby populated settlement as having a
contact. Work with the DM to decide the nature of this
contact. The contact must be related to your past as a
soldier or commander. Every time you use this power after
the first time, use the below effect.
Effect: You are easily able to find the chosen contact if you
are in the area they frequent, or are easily able to find out
if they’ve moved on from the area. If they or someone else
has made it difficult for some reason (for example, they are
in hiding, were kidn apped, they’re a criminal, or you chose
someone extremely important and busy, like an old noble
you swore your allegiance to) you gain a bonus to any
checks to find hints in the area of their location, well -
being, or to bypass the people or politics to fin d them
equal to your Wisdom modifier + 2. The contact will only
help you with information. You gain a +5 bonus to
knowledge checks for information they would reasonably
know while talking to them if they are amenable to help.
Special: You may choose this ability again even if you have
already learned it to gain additional contacts. You may
also choose a new contact if an old one dies or becomes
inaccessible.
Old War Buddy Contacts
Contacts a warlord might have left behind: the
quartermaster who now keeps a general store, the
sergeant who took over an inn, the scout who
married into a local family, the field surgeon
serving as the town healer, or the officer who
traded a commission f
or a seat on the council.
Pick someone whose current trade gives them a
reason to hear things.

definitions.fullText:
Quickly Know Your
Warlord Utility 6
Enemy
Ten minutes watching a foe move, breathe, and bluster tells you
most of what you need to know about them.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Gathering Information, Martial
Practice
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 10 minutes
Effect: Choose one creature you observed or interacted
with, outside of combat, for the power’s cast time. You
learn certain information about its capabilities compared
to your own: the DM tells you whether the creature is your
equal, superior, or inferior with regard to one of the
following of your choice — Strength, Dexterity,
Constitution, Wisdom, Intelligence, Charisma, Armor
Class, Fortitude, Reflex, or current hit points.

definitions.name: A Harsh Lesson in Skill Challenges
definitions.fullText:
A Harsh Lesson in
Warlord Utility 10
Skill Challenges
Losses can be just as important as victories. You teach an ally
how to harness a loss; as demotivating as it may be in the
moment, you know it will come in handy in the future.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: Your party fails a skill challenge or a group skill
check.
Effect: You gain experience points as if the party had
succeeded at the skill challenge. You may also choose one
ally. That ally may choose to lose a healing surge if they
have any; if they do, they gain 1 action point.
Learning from a Loss
A failed skill challenge should still move the story
— the party reaches the ruins late, or talks their
way in but owes someone a favor. This power
rewards the table for playing the failure out rather
than reloading it, so hand out the experience and
let the consequence stand.

Conscience of
Good

and bad actions.

ally of the target’s at some point in the future, the target
gets a feeling in their conscience that it will, and of who it
will affect. They do not learn why.

needing to.

flashback or echoing words of wisdom.

keep this die until the end of their next extended rest or
until it is spent.

ever thought possible.

reroll it and take the second result. Their short rests also

spent. These effects last until the end of your allies’ next
extended rest or until you are resurrected, whichever
comes first.

Battle Retrospective

Meeting
Before anyone gets comfortable, you walk the party back throu
the fight blow by blow. Next time you meet these things, nobod
will be guessing.

No Action
Personal

rest after a combat encounter.
Effect: Choose a number of enemy types from your last
encounter equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum
of 1). In your next encounter, you and your allies deal an
extra 1d6 damage with your attacks against enemies of
those types, which increases by another 1 d6 on a critical
hit. This extra damage is not added to ongoing damage or
to flat damage from zones.
In addition, you and your allies gain a +1 bonus to your
defenses against attacks from those enemies. These effects
end after your next short or extended rest.

definitions.name: Defensive Spin
definitions.fullText:
Defensive Spin
Warlord Utility 16
Your haft becomes a blur, batting aside anything that comes ne
you or the people at your shoulder
— and it bites the air hard
enough to carry you down gently, too.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Stance, Physical
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be wielding a spear, a staff, or a
polearm.
Effect: Until the stance ends, you and each ally adjacent to
you gain a +2 power bonus to AC and Reflex. This bonus
does not apply to an ally who is between you and an
enemy targeting them. This stance can be sustained for up
to 1 hour while you are out of combat , instead of 5
minutes. You cannot use other weapon powers or make
other weapon attacks while you are in this stance.
In addition, while you are falling you slowly glide downward
like a landing helicopter. While falling in this stance, you
may choose to gain a fly speed of 1, but at the end of each
of your turns you fall up to 3 squares.
Special: If you are wielding a reach weapon, extend the
range of your AC and Reflex bonuses by 1 square. Also,
you do not take falling damage for a fall of 3 squares or
less.

definitions.name: Efficient Break
definitions.fullText:
Efficient Break
Warlord Utility 16
You efficiently tell everyone to get a quick breather, direct some
people to patch up others, grab some water, slap them on the
back, and with a reluctant groan, you all keep moving. There's n
time to stop, not right now.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Rest, Martial Practice
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: There are no enemies that you or your allies
can currently see, and you are not aware of any invisible
enemies in your immediate vicinity. The combat is
essentially over, or between waves or phases.
Cast Time: 30 seconds
Effect: You and all of your allies who can see or hear you
and who are not currently in combat may each make a DC
22 Endurance check. You may then take a short rest. This
rest lasts 30 seconds instead of 5 minutes. Every ally who
succeeded on the Endurance check also benefits from this
short rest.
You and your allies may not use Rest powers during this
short rest. You may, however, end any negative effects
that end at the end of an encounter, keep any positive
effects that end at the end of an encounter, and spend
healing surges and gain the other b enefits of a short rest.
You may also choose to roll a second Endurance check. If
you roll a 20 or higher, the short rest takes only 10
seconds — one round of combat time — such as when
enemies are about to bust down the door and even 30
seconds is too long. If you roll a 9 or low er, you do not
benefit from the short rest at all.

definitions.name: I Read Your Book!
definitions.fullText:
I Read Your Book!
Warlord Utility 16
You’ve studied this enemy — their campaigns, their doctrine, their
bad habits. You know what they are about to do because they
have done it before.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Gathering Information,
War
Standard Action
Personal
Effect: Make an Intelligence ability check, or a Tactics skill
check if that skill exists in your campaign. Based on the
result, you may ask a number of questions about an
enemy, force, or faction. You must already know
something about the subject, either by havi ng fought them
before, by researching them, or perhaps by discussing
them with someone who has known them well. If you are
learning secondhand by discussing them with someone
else, or by reading a vague book on the topic, the check
takes a -2 penalty. The questions must relate either to the
subject’s current capability or to what they are going to do
next, and must be able to be intuited, although the DM is
encouraged to allow wild leaps of logic.
Check Result

* If you roll less than a 10, you don’t glean any new
information, but you gain a +2 bonus the next time you
use this power against that same subject.
Inspiring: Add a bonus to the check equal to your Charisma
modifier.
Insightful: Add a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom
modifier.
Tactical: Double your Intelligence modifier for the check.
Special: This power can’t be used on the same subject
twice, unless you have gained new information about
them somehow (fighting a new enemy from that force,
reading a new source, talking to a new creature with a
different perspective, and so on).

definitions.name: Leading the Planning Session
definitions.fullText:
Leading the Planning
Warlord Utility 16
Session
You spread out what you know, assign the jobs, and drill the pla
until everyone can do their part half asleep.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Rest
No Action
Personal
Trigger: You and your allies are taking a short rest.
Effect: Choose a task related to a skill that you or an ally is
trained in. You and all of your allies gain a +5 bonus to
skill checks and ability checks related to that task. This
bonus lasts until that character has made a roll with that
skill, or until the end of your next short or extended rest.
The task must be fairly specific: climb a particular wall, get
past a door, negotiate with someone, track a specific
monster or person, and so on. Most skill challenges can
serve as a task.

everyone else sleep like they've earned it.

they have finished the rest. An ally does not gain this
bonus healing surge if they already have more healing
surges than their maximum.
Bravura: You may gain the bonus healing surge yourself
instead of one of your allies.

definitions.fullText:
Coordinated Home
Warlord Utility 22
Defense
You endlessly think about different ways your home territory ca
be attacked, and have prepared your staff, soldiers, or party to
execute these pre-planned stratagems.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Stronghold, War
Standard Action
Personal
Effect: All of your PC allies defending your home base or
stronghold from an outside attack or from internal
sabotage may spend 1 healing surge and move up to their
speed.
Stronghold: If you are using stronghold rules, this can be
used in the area of any stronghold. If you do, any NPC
staff, soldiers, or guards who work at or defend the
stronghold and who can see or hear you immediately gain
hit points equal to the highest of your Wisd om,
Intelligence, or Charisma score.
Warfare: If you are using Warfare rules and are in a Warfare
encounter, any unit that is in a space with a stronghold or
home base returns to full casualty health.
Special: You must spend a week preparing and learning an
area determined by your DM. Once that time is complete,
you can declare that area as your home base.

For each one who does, the next time they make a skill or ability check using that skill or ability, they may use t he demonstrating ally’s bonus instead of their own, with an extra bonus equal to your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier. This effect ends before your next short or extended rest.

definitions.name: Hooooold
definitions.fullText:
Hooooold
Warlord Utility 22
You’re used to timing group actions with your volleys, which can
carry on to other coordinated actions, too.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, War, Battle Preparation
No Action
Personal
Requirement: You must have a heavy thrown weapon or a
ranged weapon.
Trigger: You ready an action or delay your turn.
Effect: All allies who also ready their action or delay their
turn to right after the same point in time get a bonus to
their attacks if you attacked, or a bonus to their skill
checks and ability checks if you used a skill or ability
check, equal to your Charisma , Intelligence, or Wisdom
modifier. If any of these allies critically hit or rolled a 20
on their skill check or ability check, they and you gain an
action point.
Warfare: If you are using Warfare rules and are in a Warfare
encounter, you may use this power at the end of your turn.
If you do, until the beginning of your next turn, any
number of other allies may delay activating one or more of
their units. For each one who d oes, they may instead
activate those units at any point during your turn - before,
after, or between you activating any of your units. They
gain a +1 bonus to any defenses and defense rolls until the
beginning of your next turn, and they get a +2 bonus to
any offensive rolls made during your turn.

definitions.name: Kinetic Coaching
definitions.fullText:
Kinetic Coaching
Warlord Utility 22
You call the correction out mid-motion — shift the grip, drop the
hips, drive from the legs — and the body listens before the mind
catches up.
Encounter + Non -Combat, Martial, Physical
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You or an ally fails a Strength, Dexterity, or
Constitution skill check.
Target: If an ally failed the skill check, this power targets
you. Otherwise, if you failed the skill check, target an ally.
Effect: The target may attempt the same skill check with a
bonus equal to 2 + your Wisdom, Charisma, or
Intelligence modifier. If they succeed, as a free action you
may apply this bonus back to the triggering creature if
they attempt that skill check again this e ncounter.

definitions.name: Retroactive Subordinate's Task
definitions.fullText:
Retroactive
Warlord Utility 22
Subordinate's Task
In your party’s moment of need, everyone looks to you. Luckily,
you already anticipated this moment, and have already had you
subordinate do something to adjust for this situation. In the
distance you hear the horn of reinforcements. Right on time.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Social
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must have an existing NPC ally who was
already established as friendly with you before your last
extended rest. You must be out of combat.
Effect: Choose a point in the past at which your character
retroactively contacted the friendly NPC ally. It could be to
contact them for some reason, or to have them contact a
different creature or faction. Giving them a task does not
guarantee their success, but it does give them the
opportunity to have acted at any point before the present
scene, as if your character had anticipated the current
situation.

definitions.name: Signal Arrow

Signal Arrow
Warlord Utility 22
The shot goes up, and everyone downrange knows exactly what
means and exactly where to look.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Weapon, War
Standard Action
Ranged weapon
Requirement: You must have a ranged weapon or a heavy
thrown weapon.
Effect: You may activate another Warlord power you have
access to and use it as if its origin were anywhere within
the range of your ranged weapon. That power can’t
damage or affect enemies, but it can affect allies. Its area
of effect is doubled, and that power is not expended.
Warfare: If you are using Warfare rules and are in a Warfare
encounter, you may apply an ability or square with an
extra space of range.

definitions.name: Unstoppable Phalanx Formation
definitions.fullText:
Unstoppable Phalanx
Warlord Utility 22
Formation
You lift your shield as an emblem as inspiring as any banner,
and then charge forward encouraging your unit to do the same
They cannot be stopped.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Stance, War
Standard Action
Close burst 60
Requirement: You must have a shield.
Target: You and each ally with a shield in the burst who can
see or hear you, and each ally adjacent to you or to them
Effect: Until the stance ends, each target gains a +2 bonus
to their defenses and to their speed, and forced movement
against them is reduced by 1 square. They cannot be
slowed, stunned, restrained, or dominated, and they
increase their charge damage by 1[W].
If you attack an enemy, or if you would be stunned,
restrained, or dominated, the stance ends instead.
Warfare: If you are using Warfare rules and are in a Warfare
encounter, you may use this to remove all negative effects
on your unit, move them 1 space, and give a +2 bonus to
their defenses until the end of your next turn.

definitions.fullText:
You Can Sleep When
Warlord Utility 22
You're Dead
Nobody is comfortable, nobody is finished, and nobody is going
argue. Five minutes. Up.
Daily + Non -Combat, Martial, Rest, Restoration
No Action
Personal
Trigger: You and your allies are taking an extended rest.
Effect: The extended rest is sped up so that it only takes the
time of a short rest (5 minutes). You still gain all the
benefits of an extended rest, except that you do not regain
this power during this extended rest, and you and your
allies each regain one less healing surge.

definitions.name: Fearful Eldritch Speech
definitions.fullText:
Fearful Eldritch Speech
Warlock Utility 2
You speak words in a tongue never meant for mortal throats.
Those who hear them without understanding them hear only th
malice underneath.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Arcane, Fear, Social, Battle
Preparation
Minor Action
Personal
Prerequisite: You must be able to speak a language other
than Common.
Effect: Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +3 bonus
to Intimidate checks against creatures that can understand
a language. You must speak a language to the creature to
benefit from this bonus, but the creature you are
intimidating can't speak the language you are speaking
when using this power. Finally, this power can't boost
Intimidate checks spoken in Common.
If this power is used out of combat but it triggers
an initiative check for some reason, on the first round of
the combat encounter those same creatures get a -2
penalty to their defenses against powers with the Fear
keyword.

definitions.name: Forbidden Knowledge Ritual
definitions.fullText:
Forbidden Knowledge
Warlock Utility 2
Ritual
You beseech your patron or one of their servants to teach you
even more forbidden knowledge, though often it comes at a pri
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual
Free Action
Personal
Special: Upon first gaining this power, choose an Arcana or
Religion ritual of level 6 or less that you can learn. You
immediately learn that ritual without having to pay the
buy cost and can cast it as if you had the Ritual Caster feat
even if you don't have it.
Trigger: You are performing the ritual you chose for this
power.
Effect: Roll twice for a skill check you are required to make
for the ritual and choose the higher result. In addition, the
ritual takes half the time to perform. However, you take 5
damage if the ritual is successful, +1 damage per level of
the ritual.
Elemental Pact: You can also use this power with Primal
rituals.

definitions.name: Minor Desiccation
definitions.fullText:
Minor Desiccation
Warlock Utility 2
You draw the moisture out of what you touch, and it crumbles t
dust and dry husk.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Arcane, Cantrip, Destruction
Standard Action
Melee touch
Target: One pool or container of water, one non -creature
plant-life, or (with the Sorcerer-King pact) one creature.
Effect: • If the target is water or a similar watery liquid that
is small, like up to 1 quart or liter, it immediately
evaporates.
• If the target plant -life is medium or smaller,
including grass, shrubbery, and so on, it withers and dies.
• If the target plant -life is large or bigger, it loses
some moisture, but it is not enough to fell most trees or
larger plants without several castings, depending on the
size.
Sorcerer-King Pact: If the target is a creature that can get
thirsty, they get a little thirsty. Or their skin dries a little. If
you made them thirsty, they will generally be compelled
to find a drink if they aren't otherwise distracted with
something important or in combat. Their physical ability
or skill checks, or your DCs in physical skill challenges
against them, get a -2 penalty until they get a drink or for
1 hour. If you targeted their skin, they get a -1 penalty to
Charisma ability checks or skill checks using their looks to
influence others for the next 1 hour.
Elemental Pact: Once you absorb the water from
something, you can later emit the water from your hands
or an implement. You can only absorb up to an amount of
water equal to the amount in a waterskin, or about 2 liters
or half a gallon or 4 pints.

definitions.name: Desiccate Plants
definitions.fullText:
Desiccate Plants
Warlock Utility 6
You level your rod at the ground and the water answers, dragge
up out of root and soil to spiral once around the implement befo
it thins away into nothing.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Implement, Destruction
Standard Action
Melee touch or Area burst 2 within 1
square
Special: When using this as a ranged power, you must be
using it through an implement you are proficient with. If
you are, you may increase the range by +1 for every +1
enhancement bonus on the implement.
Effect: • All water in the burst or one continuous amount of
water you are touching immediately evaporates, up to
about 100 gallons or 10 cubic feet. This includes water,
watery liquids, and mist. Ice and other frozen watery
liquids evaporate at half the rate.
• All non -creature plant-life within the burst or
that you touch that is medium or smaller, including grass,
shrubbery, and so on, withers and dies.
• Any plant -life within the burst that is large or
bigger loses some more moisture, but it is not enough to
fell most trees or larger plants without several castings,
depending on the size. If you touch a larger plant instead
of using the area burst, you can make it wither and die if it
is no larger than the size of your average oak tree.
Sorcerer-King Pact: You may use this twice before each
extended rest. The burst also increases by +1 when using
an implement, and the touch effect can fell even the
largest of non-magical trees.
Elemental Pact: You may use this twice before each
extended rest. You may also use this to emit the water you
absorb. You can only store up to about 20 of the gallons
you absorb this way, and you can emit it into an open
container with your hands or an implement, or make it fall
from the sky in an 8 -square cube (40 feet).

definitions.name: Ethereal Jump
definitions.fullText:
Ethereal Jump
Warlock Utility 6
A minute of muttered syllables and small precise gestures, and
then, you are simply not there. You are standing a short distanc
away.
At-Will + Non-Combat, Arcane, Teleportation, Ritual,
Exploration
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 1 minute.
Effect: You teleport 3 squares.
Dark Pact: Can teleport +1 square if your destination
square is heavily obscured by darkness or shadow.
Infernal Pact: Can teleport +1 square if your destination

definitions.fullText:
Glamor Disguise
Warlock Utility 6
You conjure fey magic to change your appearance.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Illusion, Deception
Standard Action
Personal
Target: One creature you can see that is only up to one size
larger or smaller than you.
Effect: You adopt the target's appearance until the end of
your next turn. You gain a +5 bonus to Bluff checks
related to mimicking the target. Your apparent size and
equipment matches the creature, but you gain neither the
abilities, mannerisms, or tactile or aud itory properties of
them. If anyone touches your real self through the illusion
(or fails to touch your real self if you are disguised as
someone larger than you are, for example), they will
realize you are not as you seem.
Sustain Minor: You sustain the effects until the end of your
next turn. This can be sustained up to 6 hours this way.
Fey Pact: If used out of combat, this effect lasts for up to 10
minutes before you start needing to sustain it. You may
also sustain it up to 24 hours instead of 6.

definitions.name: Knowledge from Beyond
definitions.fullText:
Knowledge from Beyond
Warlock Utility 6
You channel or consult otherworldly entities to gain increased
knowledge.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Divination,
Gathering Information
Standard Action
Personal
Cost: Take 10 damage or lose a healing surge.
Cast Time: 5 minutes.
Effect: You gain a +5 bonus to a knowledge or monster
knowledge check related to Arcana, Dungeoneering,
History, Nature, or Streetwise, or an ally gets a +3 bonus
to such a skill check. You or the ally must be trained in
that skill to receive the bonus.
Vestige Pact or Star Pact: You can use this power to boost
a skill you don't have trained, but you take an additional 5
damage in addition to whatever cost you paid for this
ritual power.

definitions.name: Magic Circle the Focused
definitions.fullText:
Magic Circle the Focused
Warlock Utility 6
You draw a circle that glows and sparks, keeping the dangerous
creature at bay for now.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Binding
Standard Action
Personal
Special: When you gain this power, choose one from the
following list of creature origins: aberrant, elemental, fey,
immortal, or shadow. This choice is permanent, but you
can change this choice on level up.
Cost: 100 gp
Cast Time: 30 minutes.
Effect: This power is identical to the Magic Circle ritual, but
can only be used against creatures of the origin you chose.
You inscribe a circle on the ground that requires 1
minute to draw per square inside the circle (and it must be
a circle). You then perform the ritual by making an Arcana
check.
An affected creature whose level is lower than
your Arcana check result minus 10 cannot pass through
the circle, affect creatures through the circle's boundary,
or affect the boundary in any way. Other creatures of an
affected origin take force damage equa l to your Arcana
check result when passing through the boundary, but
doing so breaks the circle. Unaffected creatures can take a
standard action to obscure the inscription and break the
circle.

definitions.name: Summon Eldritch Steed
definitions.fullText:
Summon Eldritch Steed
Warlock Utility 6
The shadows coalesce into something that is almost a horse,
which steps out of the darkness to carry you.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Conjuration, Ritual, Travel,
Creation
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 5 minutes.
Effect: You conjure a Large horselike Beast creature that can
be ridden by you. It has a speed of 10. The steed cannot
attack or affect other creatures in any way other than to
serve as a mount. Its defense scores are equal to yours,
although it only has 1 hit poi nt. It lasts until dismissed or
for 8 hours.
Dark Pact: The mount gains the Shadow type, immune to
all effects except damage.
Infernal Pact: The mount gains the Immortal (devil) type, it
gains health equal to your bloodied hit points, and
resistance 10 to fire damage.
Fey Pact: The mount gains the Fey type. As an encounter
power move action, it can teleport up to 5 squares.
Elemental Pact: It gains the elemental and magical beast
types (aquatic, water). It can run on water as fast as it can
run on land.
Vestige Pact: You may increase the cast time to 1 hour and
spend 200 gp in components or use 1 healing surge when
using this power to use any one of the pact bonuses from
above.

definitions.fullText:
The Logic of Madness
Warlock Utility 6
Secondary effects from your patron seep into your mind, causin
a type of magic. Sometimes it causes trouble, other times it cau
amazing leaps of logic that don't make sense, but lead to result
Encounter + Non-Combat, Arcane, Social, Gathering
Information
Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You are making a Diplomacy or Bluff check to
convince someone of something, an Insight check to learn
something about someone, a Perception or similar check
to investigate something, or are making a skill check to
gather information.
Effect: Roll a d20. On a 1 -10, you get a -5 penalty to the
triggering check. On an 11 -20, you get a +5 bonus to the

same category this encounter. If you succeed on the check,
the DM may choose to grant you one pertinent piece of
information related to the check, something your
character probably shouldn't have known but they seem
to know anyway.

definitions.name: Desiccate Creatures
definitions.fullText:
Desiccate Creatures
Warlock Utility 10
You turn the same working on living things, and what answers
the rod is the water inside them.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Implement, Destruction
Standard Action
Melee touch or Area burst 3 within 1
square
Special: When using this as a ranged power, you must be
using it through an implement you are proficient with. If
you are, you may increase the range by +1 for every +1
enhancement bonus on the implement.
Effect: All non -construct, non-undead creatures in the area
other than you, or being touched by you, have moisture
drawn from their bodies.
Make a Constitution or Charisma (whichever is
higher) vs. Fortitude attack against each creature in the
area. Each creature you hit suffers 5 damage every 1 hour
until they drink something that satiates thirst. Plant
creatures, water elementals, and other water-based
creatures take 10 damage every 30 minutes instead.
Affected creatures can ignore the effects of this
power for 1 hour by making a DC 15 Endurance check.
However, every time they succeed on this check, the DC
increases by +5 until the effect ends or until they fail the
check.
Sorcerer-King Pact: You may use this twice before each
extended rest. The burst also increases by +1 when using
an implement, and the touch effect doubles the damage
and halves the interval once more.
Elemental Pact: You may use this twice before each
extended rest. If you reduce the hit points of a water
elemental to 0 this way, you may summon a Lesser Water
Elemental (MV) with this.

definitions.name: Devil's Granted Wings
definitions.fullText:
Devil's Granted Wings
Warlock Utility 10
You grow wings for a long period of time, allowing prolonged
flight, although they get in the way and require full concentratio
preventing fighting while using them.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Polymorph, Ritual, Travel
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 30 seconds.
Effect: You grow wings for as long as you concentrate on
sustaining this power with your standard action, up to 8
hours. During this time, you gain the ability to fly with an
overland speed of 10 and a fly speed of 5, and you gain a
+2 bonus to Intimidate checks. As soon as you start to fly,
you cannot take any other actions during that flight except
to move or land. Once you land after taking flight, the
wings disappear. If the effect ends while you are in the air,
you slowly glide to the ground without taking dam age.

definitions.name: Missing Time
definitions.fullText:
Missing Time
Warlock Utility 10
They will remember the hour before, and the moment after, and
nothing of the space between.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Deception
Standard Action
Melee touch
Requirement: You are out of combat.
Target: One creature you touch that is not involved in
combat
Effect: You remove from 1 to 10 minutes of the target's
memory from within their last hour. You cannot read their
mind, so you must either pick a time frame (the last few
minutes, for example) or a specific memory you know
exists (that they met you, that they met an ally of yours, or
that they saw someone sneaking). If the creature enters
combat, they regain their memories.

Target: One creature you touch that is not involved in
combat
Effect: You remove from 1 to 10 minutes of the target's
memory from within their last hour. You cannot read their
mind, so you must either pick a time frame (the last few
minutes, for example) or a specific memory you know
exists (that they met you, that they met an ally of yours, or
that they saw someone sneaking). If the creature enters
combat, they regain their memories.

definitions.name: Remote Fey Switch
definitions.fullText:
Remote Fey Switch
Warlock Utility 10
You place a benevolent form of your curse on an ally, binding th
two of you across any distance.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Teleportation, Ritual,
Travel
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 5 minutes.
Target: One ally
Effect: You place a benevolent form of your curse on an ally.
This has no negative effects and lasts up to 8 hours. At any
point while this is on them, you or the ally may switch
places. There is a brief shimmering light during this time
and it takes about 6 -10 se conds, or about 1-2 rounds, for
the switch to happen, preventing it from catching anyone
off-guard if it happens in front of them, but generally being
a brief moment when it happens out of view.
If it happens during a battle or it triggers a battle,
and you are out of view of each other, the person who
enters is surprised for one round.
Level 21: You can increase the cast time to 1 hour
to increase the duration by up to 24 hours.

definitions.name: Ritual of Chromatic Empowerment
definitions.fullText:
Ritual of Chromatic
Warlock Utility 10
Empowerment
You take the element out of the place it collected in and put it in
yourself.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Rest, Battle
Preparation
Standard Action
Personal
Prerequisite: Elemental Pact and you have the Chromatic
Bolt power.
Requirement: You must be near a natural or near -natural
formation of your element. The DM has the final say. It
should come from the environment, but it is up to the DM.
This must be done during a rest, but before you know
what element you'll roll for on the elemental attunement
table (see Warlock Elemental Pact).
Cast Time: 5 minutes.
Effect: You perform a ritual to absorb the natural powers of
the nearby element. Until the end of your next extended
rest or you use this power again, you empower one of the
elements. As long as you are attuned to it, you gain one of
the following effects:
• Acid - When you hit with your Chromatic Bolt,
until the end of your next turn, lower the AC of one of the
creatures hit by your Chromatic Bolt by the lower of your
Charisma or Constitution modifier minus 2.
• Cold - When you hit with your Chromatic Bolt,
you may gain temporary hit points equal to the lower of
your Charisma or Constitution modifier until the
beginning of your next turn.
• Fire - Your Chromatic Bolt deals an extra 1d6
fire damage to the first target.
• Lightning - You may have your Chromatic Bolt
deal an additional 2 damage to the first target, 1 damage
to the second target, and damage equal to the lower of
your Charisma or Constitution modifier to a third creature
within 5 squares of your second targe t. If there is no other
creature within 5 squares, it may deal that damage back to
the first creature.
• Thunder - You may push the first and second
target of your Chromatic Bolt away from each other when
it hits, up to a number of squares equal to the lower of
your Charisma or Constitution modifier.
EXAMPLES OF NATURAL
ELEMENTAL FORMATIONS
Acid: a pool of acid from a laboratory experiment, an
acidic swamp, a longstanding acidic trap or hazard, a
slime’s lair, a caustic geyser, collected acid in bottles,
acid rain.
Cold: a field of ice or snow, a near
-frozen lake, a
blizzard, snowfall, hail.
Fire: a large fire (wild or long -burning), lit lanterns,
lava, a magma geyser, a large forge.
Lightning: a lightning storm, rain, a laboratory with
electricity, proximity to lots of metal or arcane
machinery, “pre-storm” static in the air, carpets or
rugs with static cling, magnetic phenomena.
Thunder: a lightning or wind storm, high wind, a
hurricane, rain, areas of extreme noise such as
industrial work sites, echoing canyons or caves.

definitions.name: Sacrificial Ritual of Reclamation
definitions.fullText:
Sacrificial Ritual of
Warlock Utility 10
Reclamation
A life given freely, or given unwillingly, buys back a working you
thought was spent.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual
Standard Action
Personal
Cost: One willing or helpless creature, sacrificed.
Cast Time: 1 hour.
Effect: Roll an Arcana or Religion check, depending on
whether the target ritual power will be Arcane or Divine
respectively. It has a DC equal to 35 - the level of the
sacrificed creature. If you succeed on the check, you or an
ally within 5 squares regains one e xpended ritual power
that is at least half that level or below (rounded down) and
uses the associated power source. This cannot be used on
creatures above level 30.

definitions.name: Shadowy Touch
definitions.fullText:
Shadowy Touch
Warlock Utility 10
Your hand becomes of shadows and misty wisps, passing throug
the physical easily while still imparting the magical effects you'v
infused into your touch.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Deception
Minor Action
Personal or Melee touch
Target: You or one creature you touch
Effect: When used out of combat, as long as the target is
even slightly distracted or looking away, your next Touch
power can be used without its target and others in the
vicinity aware you have used it on them. If they are a bit
more aware of your presence, the D M may determine you
need to use a Thievery check with an easy DC equal to the
level of the creature you're trying to use the touch power
on. If so, it gets a +5 bonus.
When used in combat, you must be hidden and
actively hiding from the enemy for this power to work on
them. It also doesn't get any +5 bonus when the DM
determines you need to use a Thievery check to activate
this power.

definitions.name: Speaking in Tongues
definitions.fullText:
Speaking in Tongues
Warlock Utility 10
The words of one tongue are taken out of a mouth and the wor
of another are put in their place.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Social
Standard Action
Personal or Melee touch
Target: You or one creature you touch
Effect: You or a creature you touch lose the ability to speak
Common, or a language of your choice if they don't speak
Common, but they gain the ability to speak and
understand a language of your choice. The target can still
understand the native language they los t during this time,
they just can't speak it or write in it. It lasts 1 hour or until
you dismiss the effect.
If used on an unwilling creature, you must hit on
an unarmed melee Constitution or Charisma vs. Will
attack.

definitions.name: Summon Eldritch Hound
definitions.fullText:
Summon Eldritch Hound
Warlock Utility 10
You conjure a hound that is only shaped like a hound, and it
takes the scent you give it.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Conjuration, Ritual,
Exploration
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 5 minutes.
Effect: You conjure a Small or Medium doglike creature to
help you track other people or things. As long as you have
a sample of the scent to give the creature, it can detect the
direction of the creature it's tracking as long as it's within
1000 feet. It also get s a +5 bonus to Perception, Survival,
or Nature checks to track the creature, or to aid others in
tracking. It lasts up to 1 hour.
The conjured creature has 1 hit point and a speed
of 7, although that is reduced to 3 when tracking.
Fey Pact: The fey hounds of the hunt are legendary for
finding their prey. The conjured creature has the fey type
and it can detect creatures with no limit, even in other
planes, if it has the scent. They last half the time, though.
Infernal Pact: The conjured creature has the Immortal
(demon) or (devil) type and is immune to fire damage but
has vulnerability 10 to radiant and cold damage. In
addition, this hell -hound will attempt to protect you. It has
max hit points equal to yours and two attacks.
Melee Attack. Constitution vs. AC. 1d6 +
Constitution modifier damage + 1d6 fire damage.
Fire Defense (encounter). Immediate Reaction
when attacked by a melee attack. Close Burst 1, target
enemies. Constitution vs. Reflex. On hit: 2d8 +
Constitution modifier fire damage.
Dark Pact: The conjured dog has the shadow type. It can
scout ahead and track for you stealthily before coming
back to let you know the way. As long as it is in darkness
or low-light, it can turn invisible as an at -will minor action.
It has a Stealth check equal to y ours +2. It disappears even
if a radiant attack misses it, though.
Elemental Pact: It lasts twice as long if summoned in terrain
related to your current elemental attunement, gains
immunity to that element, and gains the elemental type
and another type related to that element. It is not affected
by penalties related to your current eleme ntal
attunement: passing through water or similar liquids will
not penalize its tracking if it is acid or cold type, fire means
it's not stopped by strong smells by things like smoke, and
wind blowing away the scent does not stop it if it is
lightning or thunder. If the tracked object or creature
passes through terrain or a situation related to your
elemental attunement, the hound will alert you. If you
have the lightning or thunder attunement, the tracking
range doubles.
Star Pact: The creature is strange and unnerving, slipping
through the mind and causing small bouts of madness and
small twists of fate. Onlookers' eyes will slide right off it.
Unless the creature brings attention to itself, you can roll
Stealth vs. Insight to have people you are interacting with
not notice the hound.
Vestige Pact: You may increase the cast time to 1 hour and
spend 400 gp in components or use 2 healing surges
when using this power to use any one of the pact bonuses
from above.
