definitions.name: Tentacle From the Other Side
definitions.fullText:
Tentacle From the Other
Warlock Utility 10
Side
You create a portal just large enough for a tentacle to poke
through and start causing havoc. Whether it's to guard a door,
cause a distraction, or simply to retrieve something for you, the
tentacle obeys.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Conjuration, Ritual,
Creation
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 1 round, 1 minute, 10 minutes, or 1 hour.
Duration: 1 round, 10 minutes, 1 hour, or 6 hours,
respectively.
Effect: You make a tentacle sprout from the ground or a
wall. It has a range of 4 squares. In addition to preventing
access to that square by taking up space (so if put on the
ground, no one can step in that square for example), it will
also attempt to grapple nea rby creatures, hurt them, and
then drag them into the portal with it. Creatures who are
dragged into the portal will not be in play until the effect
ends. This ritual automatically ends if the tentacle dies. It
has an amount of health equal to your hit poi nts + 10.
You can also command the tentacle to grab
specific enemies or objects for you, interact with the
environment, and so on. It will usually expect a reward for
that.
Standard Melee Attack: Melee 4; Constitution or
Charisma vs. Reflex. On hit: 2d8 + Constitution or
Charisma modifier damage and the target is grabbed.
Swing Attack (Standard): Close Burst 2;
Constitution or Charisma vs. Reflex. On hit: 2d8 +
Constitution or Charisma modifier damage.
Immediate Reaction: If bloodied or critically hit, it
will retreat into its portal, becoming untargetable and
invisible. If it does this, it will let go of any creature it's
grabbing. The portal will re -open, and the tentacle will re -
emerge at the beginnin g of its next turn.
Sustain Standard: The tentacle will sustain the grab on a
grabbed target, deal 1d8 damage to them, and pull them
1 square closer to it. If they reach the tentacle's square,
the enemy will disappear until this effect ends.
Instinctive Effect: If you haven't given the tentacle any
commands by the end of your turn, it attacks the last
creature to attack it. Otherwise, it attacks the nearest
creature it can attack and attempts to grab. If it can't do
that, it will destroy nearby objects or do a Sw ing Attack,
keeping enemies afraid to get close.

you can think of it as lasting 6 seconds or enough for one
action. In combat, you must use your whole turn to cast it,
and you must keep casting it until the beginning of your
next turn. It then lasts from the beginning of that turn until
the beginning of your next turn. If used in this way, you
may take 3 damage to regain this power.

definitions.name: Vestige Memory
definitions.fullText:
Vestige Memory
Warlock Utility 10
Something that has already read every book in a dead language
lends you the trick of it.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Social, Gathering
Information
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 10 minutes.
Effect: Choose a language. You are able to read and write in
the chosen language for the next 1 hour. You are also able
to speak in and understand the language fluently.
Vestige Pact: The duration extends to 24 hours and you are
able to store any text you read in the chosen language
during this time into your vestige's memory, allowing
perfect recall, search, and analysis of it later. You are also
able to allow deeper understanding of i t by equipping a
vestige that understands it better. For the next 1 hour, you
are able to answer up to 3 questions others ask you about
the text as if you were a native person from that culture,
even if it's from long ago. Gain a +5 bonus to History and
related skill checks related to the writing when answering
questions others ask you about it during this time, for the
first 3 questions you are asked at least.

definitions.name: Billowing Darkness
definitions.fullText:
Billowing Darkness
Warlock Utility 16
You create a smoky darkness that fills up the current space you
are in.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Zone, Deception
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must be indoors.
Effect: You create a zone of darkness that fills up the current
room, or closest thing to a room, you are in. It's magical
darkness that smothers all sources of light that are
mundane or from a magical item with a level lower than
you (including items that don't h ave a level, such as sun
rods). It stops at the edge of doors and similar dividers,
even if they are open. You gain darkvision while in this
zone.

definitions.name: Curse Item
definitions.fullText:
Curse Item
Warlock Utility 16
You infuse an item with dark energy, condemning whoever is
holding it to the dangers of your magic.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Binding, Battle
Preparation
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 1 minute.
Effect: You place a version of your curse on an object. It
lasts until you dismiss it as a minor action, place it on a
different object, or enter a combat with someone holding
it and place your warlock's curse on them. Those
attempting to detect this energy from t he item get a +2
bonus to their Arcana check. Other than that, you have no
bonuses to tracking the object, although you are aware if it
still exists and is whole or broken or destroyed.
Whoever is holding, wielding, or carrying the
object is afflicted by your curse, although they are not
aware if it's solely through the item. If a combat encounter
begins with them, they are afflicted by your item curse as
long as they are holding it when initiative is rolled. This is
the same as your normal curse in all ways, except that 1) it
only gives +1d6 damage, and 2) it stacks with your normal
curse (allowing it to increase the damage die of your curse
by an additional 1d6 this way).
Whoever is holding the item is also aware of some
negative vibes, although they may not be sure why. You
get a +2 bonus to Intimidate checks against them. The
curse can be removed by anything that removes curses
and some other purification effects.

definitions.name: Dark Hole Ritual
definitions.fullText:
Dark Hole Ritual
Warlock Utility 16
You draw a circle on the ground, and it opens into somewhere
else.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Creation
Standard Action
Personal
Cost: 500 gp
Cast Time: 1 minute to 8 hours.
Effect: You draw a circle on the ground, conjuring magic
that turns it into a deep, dark hole of blackness. Objects
placed inside of it disappear after being more than about a
foot from the surface, but you can still feel them to bring
them out. It is at minimum 1 foot wide and 1 foot deep.
Any larger requires increased cast time and an Arcana
check. The hole is permanent until you use this ritual
power somewhere else or dismiss it. It will move any
creatures or objects in the hole to the new location once
this is used again while a hole still exists. It can't be
dismissed while objects or creatures are still in it.

definitions.name: King's Command
definitions.fullText:
King's Command
Warlock Utility 16
You infuse your words with power, and it crushes any doubt or
refusal from their mind.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Charm, Social
Standard Action
Melee Touch
Effect: You give a command to a creature that can hear you
and that you are touching. If the creature is hostile or
otherwise tries to avoid being touched, you must first
succeed on a Charisma vs. Will attack to use the rest of
this power.
Make a Diplomacy or Intimidate check with a +5
power bonus, with a DC equal to that creature's Will. If
you succeed, they must follow the command, even if they
normally wouldn't. Self-preservation, their own attitude or
reasonableness or previous thoughts or personality won't
stop them from fulfilling it. However, they will attempt a
saving throw to escape if it threatens their self -
preservation.
They will follow it for the next 10 minutes or until
they fulfill it. If the action was reasonable, they will
probably think they did it. If it is not, they may realize
what happened. It ends automatically if they take damage.
Sorcerer-King Pact: A one-word command gets a +10
bonus. Also, either way, it lasts up to 1 hour or until they
fulfill the command.
Fey Pact: If they attempt a saving throw, instead you may
roll a Diplomacy or Intimidate check vs. their Will again
and use that as the result.

definitions.name: Lesser Eye of the Warlock
definitions.fullText:
Lesser Eye of the Warlock
Warlock Utility 16
A smaller third eye opens, and you borrow another creature's
senses.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Arcane, Scrying
Standard Action
Ranged 20 or Melee Touch
Target: One creature
Effect: You see through the target's eyes, hear through their
ears, and smell through their nose. The target is not aware
that you are doing so. You do not have line of sight and
line of effect from the target for your attacks. During this
time, you lose perception of your own senses. This lasts for
up to 5 minutes or until you end the connection.
If this is used from melee touch range, the effect
lasts up to 24 hours or until you dismiss it, and you do not
lose your senses immediately. Instead, you keep them, and
during the duration of the effect you can switch between
your own perceptions and the target's at will as a minor
action.

definitions.name: Magic Circle Against All
definitions.fullText:
Magic Circle Against All
Warlock Utility 16
You draw a circle that glows and sparks, keeping even mundane
dangerous creatures at bay.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Binding
Standard Action
Personal
Cost: 200 gp
Cast Time: 1 hour.
Effect: This power is identical to the Magic Circle ritual, but
can only be used against all creatures, regardless of type or
origin.
You inscribe a circle on the ground that requires 1
minute to draw per square inside the circle (and it must be
a circle). You then perform the ritual by making an Arcana
check.
An affected creature whose level is lower than
your Arcana check result minus 10 cannot pass through
the circle, affect creatures through the circle's boundary,
or affect the boundary in any way. Other creatures of an
affected origin take force damage equa l to your Arcana
check result when passing through the boundary, but
doing so breaks the circle. Unaffected creatures can take a
standard action to obscure the inscription and break the
circle.

definitions.fullText:
Recouping Arcane
Warlock Utility 16
Backlash
Magic does not come back for free. You take the cost out of
yourself.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Restoration
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 1 minute.
Effect: You regain one encounter or daily Arcane Non -
Combat power of level 16 or lower. You take 5 damage if
the level of the power is 6 or lower, 10 damage if the level
is 10 or lower, and 20 damage if the level of it is higher
than 10. This damage bypasses tempo rary hit points.
Dark Pact: A willing ally within 1 square of you may choose
to take the damage, plus an additional 5 damage, instead.

definitions.name: Sacrifice Ally
definitions.fullText:
Sacrifice Ally
Warlock Utility 16
You have nothing left to offer but your lives. It's time to make it
count.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Restoration
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You must have a bladed or piercing weapon
in hand.
Cast Time: 10 minutes.
Target: One willing or helpless allied PC or an allied
creature you care about
Effect: Kill the target. Choose one of the following effects:
• The next ritual you are performing or
participating in before your next extended rest is now free
to cast and takes half the time.
• You or an ally regains an expended daily Non -
Combat power.
• You and all allies gain 1 healing surge and heal
a number of hit points equal to your surge value.
• You and all allies with 0 action points gain 1
action point.

participating in before your next extended rest is now free

• You or an ally regains an expended daily Non -
Combat power.
• You and all allies gain 1 healing surge and heal
a number of hit points equal to your surge value.
• You and all allies with 0 action points gain 1
action point.

definitions.name: Shade Door Shortcut
definitions.fullText:
Shade Door Shortcut
Warlock Utility 16
The Shadowfell is closer than it looks, and it will lend you a
hallway.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Teleportation, Ritual,
Travel
Standard Action
Ranged 5
Cost: 100 gp
Cast Time: 1 hour.
Effect: This ritual power can be used twice before it is
expended. The first time it is used you create a shadowy
door. It's about the size of a normal door. It cannot be
opened until you create a second door. The next time you
use this power, you create another s hadowy door.
Creatures can instantly travel between them by using a
minor action to open the door and a move action to step
through. It counts as a teleport, but the user does not have
to see the other side.
Once a door has been created, it lasts forever until
dismissed, or destroyed in some way. Dismissing a shade
door takes a 1 minute ritual if you are within 5 squares of
it, otherwise it takes a 1 hour ritual. As long as a shade
door is created from this po wer and still exists, you cannot
regain this power. You must dismiss one or both of your
old portals in order to regain this power.
Dark Pact: You and allied creatures exit the shade doors
with a +5 bonus to Stealth checks until the end of their
next turn. It is also hard to see the doors if they are in
darkness or low -light. A DC 20 Perception check is
required, and it is invisible in darkness ( even to creatures
with darkvision).
Fey Pact: Whenever you or an allied creature teleports with
this power, you may have them appear in a random
square within 3 squares of the exit, instead of in that
square.
Infernal Pact: Whenever an enemy creature uses your
shade doors, they take 1d6 fire damage upon exiting.
Star Pact: They see maddening visions. Creatures are dazed
upon exiting for one turn.

definitions.name: Summon Infernal Advisor
definitions.fullText:
Summon Infernal Advisor
Warlock Utility 16
Through painstaking research and preparation, you prepare a
valuable offering for a powerful, knowledgeable being, such as
demigod, demon, devil, or fae. Your offering earns you an
audience with the being, which appears in a magic circle,
unfriendly, but may be willing to help with the right words.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Binding, Gathering
Information, Social
Standard Action
Personal
Cost: 10,000 gp
Cast Time: 8 hours.
Effect: You draw a magic circle and summon a powerful
extraplanar entity in it that can offer you information.
While in the circle, no one outside the circle has line of
effect to it and it does not have line of effect to you.
You must succeed on a skill challenge to obtain
the information you desire from that entity. This challenge
might be against Bluff, Diplomacy, or Intimidate,
depending on the creature. The complexity of the
challenge and the difficulty of the DCs are up to the
creature you are summoning and the difficulty of the
information you are trying to obtain, but they are generally
Complexity 3 and medium DC.
The offering may help move a creature that is in
an evil or hostile state into a more neutral state, willing to
hear you out. But one would be wise to remember that all
such entities have agendas of their own, and their nature
might color the information a nd advice they provide. If
you can successfully convince them, they will try to be
helpful to you, but it will be in their own way.
When you complete the ritual power, you can
designate up to eight other participants who can also
speak with the entity and contribute to the skill challenge.

definitions.name: We're All Mad Down Here
definitions.fullText:
We're All Mad Down Here
Warlock Utility 16
While others think you mad, you've only gained knowledge
beyond their understanding, allowing you to perceive the logic o
things without logic, and the sense in things without sense.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Arcane, Social
Minor Action
Personal
Effect: You are able to speak to animals for the next 1 hour
or until you dismiss this power. You get a +2 bonus to
Diplomacy and Nature checks with them.
Infernal Pact: You are able to speak Supernal. When you
speak this language, you get a +5 bonus when speaking to
angels, demons, devils, and other immortals that speak it
as a native language and a +5 bonus to understanding
their strange world through knowledge checks.
Fey Pact: You are able to speak Elven. When you speak this
language, you get a +5 bonus when speaking to fey, elves,
and beasts, and you are able to use this language to speak
to constructs and animate creatures, even ones that
normally do not speak any language. If in the Feywild, you
can even speak to plants and objects.
Dark Pact: You are able to speak Elven. When you speak
this language, you get a +5 bonus when speaking to fey,
elves, and certain beasts (spiders, bats, bugs, and snakes).
If in the Shadowfell, you are able to speak to undead,
ghosts, and other such creatures, even ones who are
animate or normally do not speak a language.
Elemental Pact: You are able to speak Primordial. When
you speak this language, you gain a +5 bonus when
speaking to elementals, archons, and efreets, even ones
that normally do not speak any language.

definitions.name: Bottomless Hole
definitions.fullText:
Bottomless Hole
Warlock Utility 22
You can create a portal to endless blackness, a portable hole wi
no end. Where it leads to is a mystery, and you definitely can't
retrieve people or items from such a hole. But sometimes you ne
a bottomless pit.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Creation
Standard Action
Personal
Cost: 50 gp per 1 ft diameter
Cast Time: 8 hours.
Effect: You draw a circle on the ground, conjuring magic
that turns it into a deep, dark hole of blackness, similar to
the Dark Hole Ritual, but this one seemingly has no end.
Objects placed inside of it disappear after being more than
about a foot from the surface, and seem to keep falling
forever. It is at minimum 1 foot wide, and a max of 20 feet
wide.
A successful Arcana check with a DC of 40 is
required to use this power. If you fail, you can transition
into making this a Dark Hole Ritual if you have that ritual
or ritual power (Warlock 16), using the result of that
Arcana check as the result for that effect.
This hole is permanent until you use this ritual
power somewhere else or dismiss it. It can be dismissed
while objects or creatures are still in it.
Dark Pact: You can make a temporary version with less
time. The cast time becomes 20 minutes, but it only lasts
1 hour afterwards. The cost increases to 100 gp per 1 ft.
The size is from 1 ft up to 5 ft diameter.
Fey Pact: You are able to redirect the hole to fall into a
portion of the Feywild as a minor action. When used this
way, anything put in the pit since it was last created or
dismissed is redirected to the Feywild as well. You can
jump into the hole to go there, use it to store stuff in a
glade there, etc. As a minor action, you can change it back
to a bottomless pit.
Elemental Pact: You are able to connect the hole into one
of the Elemental Planes of Chaos as a minor action, and
back. When used this way, it becomes a vertical stream of
chaotic elemental magic energy. As a standard action, or
also sometimes at random if the DM decides it, the pit
shoots out from 100 feet (20 squares) to 1,000 feet (200
squares), a burst of energy that deals damage of the same
type as your current elemental affinity. It deals 3d10
damage per 5 feet of diameter of the hole to any creature
caught in the geyser during this blast.

definitions.name: Curse of Madness
definitions.fullText:
Curse of Madness
Warlock Utility 22
Your hand begins to glow and a symbol appears on it. "No,
please. Not my mind. Anything but that!" They beg, but to no
avail.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Psychic, Binding
Standard Action
Melee Touch
Target: One sentient creature. Cannot be animated or a
construct.
Attack: Make a Charisma or Constitution attack vs. Will. If
the creature is at all aware of this happening or is in
combat, they get a +5 bonus to their Will defense and you
get a -5 penalty to your attack.
Hit: The creature begins to get affected by a type of insanity.
They are prone to babbling and mumbling, or spouting
incoherent sentences at inopportune times. They are also
harder to have a straightforward conversation or use logic
with. They get a -2 penalty to Diplomacy, Bluff, Insight,
and other social checks, and other people's attempts to
use such checks to sway them get a -2 penalty. They make
a saving throw to end the effect at the end of every
extended rest, and it works like a disease track. Successful
saving throws bring them closer to sane, failed saving
throws make them more insane. There is no max duration.
After the first failed saving throw, they begin to
lose some memories. Whenever they attempt to recall
something important, they must make a saving throw. If
they fail, they do not remember. They also get a -5 penalty
to Intelligence and Knowledge checks.
After the second failed saving throw, they lose all
memories of their previous self and begin to adopt a new
personality or new memories that aren't real. They will
begin to wander to random places, see random visions or
just random sounds, and may think t hey're someone
they're not.
After the third failed saving throw, the effect
becomes much more permanent. They make the save to
end after every month instead of every extended rest and
the saving throw gets a -2 penalty. After one year, the
effect is permanent.
Star Pact: You are able to imbue this curse into runes or
words that trigger when read. Once triggered, the curse is
removed from the item. You also get a +2 bonus to try to
get information from them instead of a -2 penalty.
Fey Pact: You get a +2 bonus to sway them, instead of a -2
penalty.
Dark Pact or Infernal Pact: The target becomes violently
mad. They are more likely to attack people who get too
close once they've lost their memories, rather than just
wander or mumble.
Vestige Pact: You send vestiges to haunt them. They get a -
1 penalty to their saving throws on this power.
DM NOTE ON CURSE OF
MADNESS
The DM may add a random trait to the insanity by
rolling on the madness table from D&D 5th Edition.

definitions.name: Mummify
definitions.fullText:
Mummify
Warlock Utility 22
You prepare the corpse: Removing unnecessary organs; soaking
the body in preservatives and embalming oils; wrapping it up
with linen wraps and amulets intended to ward away danger;
before finally adding a resin finish to keep the body properly
sealed from moisture. When all is said and done, the body has
now become a mummy.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Creation, Warding
Standard Action
Personal
Cost: 250 gp
Cast Time: 1 hour.
Effect: You prepare a corpse that is mostly whole and has
been dead for less than a century to turn into a mummy.
Until the spell is dispelled somehow, the mummy is
indefinitely protected from decay, can't become undead
by normal means, and cannot be raised from t he dead, as
its organs are transported to a protective vessel of your
choice and location.
Once the vessel containing its organs is returned
to the corpse, it can be raised from the dead, no matter
how much time has passed. Other special rituals may
return a corpse and not need the organs, though.
When you complete this ritual power, you may
make an Arcana check to set certain conditions that cause
the mummy to return and defend its surroundings. You
can also set certain conditions for creatures not to activate
the mummy, such as by speaking aloud a certain
password. When the conditions are met, the mummy will
temporarily rise as an undead creature to defend its
surroundings. It will not move further than 30 squares
(150 feet) from its place of burial. When the conditions for
its animation are no lon ger satisfied, the mummy will set
the order of its surroundings back to rights as best it can,
before re-entombing itself back in its resting place.
The creature rises as a normal mummy, which
requires 250 gp components and an Arcana check DC of
15. They have Darkvision, a speed of +4, immunity to
charm, disease, resistance 10 to necrotic and poison, but
vulnerable 10 to fire, and any creature that re duces it to 0
hit points is affected by your Warlock's Curse.
Mummy: HP 100. AC 22, Fort 24, Ref 19, Will 23.
Melee attack: +13 vs. Fortitude. On hit: 11 damage, grabs
the target (escape DC 20), and if the target is already
grabbed, deal an additional 10 necrotic damage. They are
affected by mummy rot.
Vestige Pact: The mummy has increased sentience, possibly
even having some memories from their previous life. They
can also travel indefinitely from their tomb, but they
always have a desire to return, and can only do an
extended rest there.
Elemental Pact: The mummy has immunity to the damage
of your current elemental affinity. In addition, it deals an
extra 1d6 damage of that damage type with its melee
attacks.
Sorcerer-King Pact: You can instead make them rise as a
mummy lord, but it requires 2,500 gp components
instead, and an Arcana check DC of 30. They all have the
same traits as above.
Mummy Lord: HP 250. AC 30. Fort 28, Ref 24,
Will 26. Melee attack: +20 vs. AC. On hit: 18 damage, and
the target is immobilized until the end of their next turn.
Standard Action Mummy's Curse: Close burst 10; +16 vs.
Will; all enemies within the burst cont ract level 14
mummy rot (Endurance improve DC 24, maintain DC 19,
worsen DC 18).

When all is said and done, the body has now become a mummy.

magic show itself.

the target area. If you are already aware the magic is of an
arcane source, you gain a +4 bonus instead.

definitions.name: Specialty Ritual
definitions.fullText:
Specialty Ritual
Wizard Utility 2
One ritual has become second nature to you, and your hands fin
the shortcuts your notes never mention.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual
Free Action
Personal
Requirement: You are performing the chosen ritual.
Special: When you pick this power, choose one ritual you
know of a level equal to or lower than your level. You may
replace the chosen ritual whenever you gain a level; the
new ritual must be 10th level or lower, and still equal to
or lower than your level. You can not choose the Brew
Potion or Enchant Magic Item rituals.
Effect: You cast the chosen ritual without expending any of
the ritual's gold piece component cost. Any focus item the
ritual requires must still meet its minimum cost. You and
any allies assisting you take a -2 penalty to any skill check
required by or affected by the ritual.

Wizard Utility 6
While you may not know the exact ritual, you know the base
theory well enough, and can provide help making it more efficie
as long as you're told vague instructions about where to draw t
chalk or where to place the candles.

Standard Action
Ranged 5
Requirement: An ally is performing a ritual.
Effect: Choose one benefit: the ritual costs 25% fewer
components, or it takes 25% less time to perform. This
counts as you assisting with the ritual. You cannot assist
the ritual in any other way.

definitions.name: Forging Flame
definitions.fullText:
Forging Flame
Wizard Utility 6
You coax a flame past what its fuel could ever give it, and hold i
there.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Fire, Ritual, Creation
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 5 minutes.
Effect: You stoke a flame with your magic, hot enough to
create items without a proper forge, for 24 hours. You or a
smith still need the proper blacksmith tools and materials,
or an approximation of them, but once obtained the work
can be done anywhere. You can a lso use this flame to
weld two metal items together, as long as you can hold
them together for 1 minute. Breaking them apart
afterward requires a Strength check against a Hard DC for
your level when you used this power, +5.

definitions.name: Invisible Object
definitions.fullText:
Invisible Object
Wizard Utility 6
You draw the light around it until there is nothing left to see.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Illusion, Deception
Standard Action
Melee touch or Ranged 5
Target: One object weighing no more than 500 pounds
Effect: The object becomes invisible until the end of your
next turn. If you cast this as a melee touch effect, the
invisibility instead lasts 10 minutes or until you dismiss it.
If the object becomes part of an attack or a similar
offensive action, the invisibili ty ends.
Sustain Standard: If the target is within 5 squares of you,
the invisibility persists until the end of your next turn. If
this was originally cast as melee touch, the target needs to
be within 20 squares instead, and it can be sustained for
up to an additional 10 minutes.

definitions.name: Protracted Jump
definitions.fullText:
Protracted Jump
Wizard Utility 6
You or an ally are able to jump great distances for a longer
amount of time through a slight manipulation of the spell.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Arcane, Physical, Exploration
Standard Action
Melee touch
Prerequisite: You have the Jump power (Wizard 2).
Target: You or one creature
Effect: The target can use a move action to jump up to 6
squares or up to its speed, whichever is lower, without
having to make an Athletics check. This lasts for up to 1
minute, although it lasts only until the end of the next
round if you or the target are in or enter a combat
encounter.

definitions.fullText:
Arcane Ritual Expert
Wizard Utility 10
You have done this so many times that your pockets have starte
keeping what you need: eye of newt, bat guano, a pinch of
something you would rather not name.

Free Action
Personal
Trigger: You are performing an Arcana ritual of 9th level or
lower.

ritual's gold piece component cost. Any focus item the
ritual requires must still meet its minimum cost. Instead,

the ritual does not require a skill check, you can make one
anyway to try to gain this benefit. You cannot use this
power on any ritual that creates or enchants an item, su ch
as Brew Potion or Enchant Magic Item.

definitions.name: Mass Animation
definitions.fullText:
Mass Animation
Wizard Utility 10
The room stands up all at once and waits to be told what it is fo
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Transmutation, Exploration
Standard Action
Close Burst 20
Target: Up to 10 nonmagical objects within the burst that
are not fastened down or held by a creature. Medium
objects count as two, Large objects count as four, and
Huge objects count as eight. You cannot animate Huge or
larger objects.
Effect: Each target animates until the end of your next turn,
hovering above the ground with a fly speed of 5. You may
immediately move all target objects up to their speed.
While a target is animated by this power, you can move it
5 squares through the air, and i t retains the ability to fly
and hover. You may also use a minor action to have any
number of target objects begin a mundane task related to
their normal function: brooms begin sweeping, pots begin
stirring, and so on.
You cannot make attacks with the objects, even if
it appears you can. A sword may flick and slice in the air,
but with no aim or power behind it.
Sustain Move: The animation persists until the end of your
next turn for objects within 100 squares (about 500 feet),
and you may move all target objects up to 5 squares.

definitions.name: Mirror Image
definitions.fullText:
Mirror Image
Wizard Utility 10
Three duplicate images of you appear, imitating your actions
perfectly and confusing your enemies.
Daily + Non-Combat, Combat, Arcane, Illusion,
Deception
Minor Action
Personal
Special: This does not affect enemies that can see through
illusions or that have blindsight.
Effect: Three duplicate images of yourself appear in your
space. Whenever you are targeted by a melee or ranged
attack, you gain a +2 power bonus to all your defenses for
each duplicate image you have active, up to a +6 bonus.
Each time a melee or ranged attack mi sses you, unless the
attacker rolled an automatic miss, one of your duplicate
images disappears, and the bonus granted by this power
decreases by 2. When the bonus reaches 0, all your
images are gone and the power ends. Otherwise, the
effect lasts for 1 hour. During a short rest, if you have at
least 1 but fewer than 3 duplicates, you gain 1 more
duplicate image.
Enemies may also target you with melee or
ranged attacks that normally target more than one enemy,
targeting you an extra time for each duplicate image you
have.
New Level 10 Utility Spells

definitions.name: Beneficient Transformation
definitions.fullText:
Beneficient
Wizard Utility 16
Transformation
Tendrils of wispy energy surround your foe, assessing and
stealing away some essential aspect of its being for your own us
Daily + Combat, Arcane, Transmutation
Minor Action
Ranged 10
Target: You and one ally, or up to two allies
Effect: Choose an enemy you can see. If you chose only one
target, it gains up to three of the following benefits until
the end of the encounter. If you chose two targets, each
target gains up to two of the following benefits instead.
Movement: If the enemy has a climb speed, a fly speed, or a
swim speed, the target gains that movement mode and
speed.
Resist: If the enemy has resistance or immunity to a damage
type, the target gains resist 10 to the same damage type.
Senses: If the enemy has low -light vision, darkvision,
blindsight, or tremorsense, the target gains that sense.
Attacks: If the enemy has hit you or an ally with a non -
weapon, non-implement attack during this encounter, the
target gains access to that attack and undergoes the
physical changes needed to make it, such as growing claws
or fangs. The target uses the enemy's attack bonus,
damage, and other statistics for that attack. The change
grants no other benefit; wings grown for a wing gust attack
do not let the target fly, for example. The target cannot
gain arcane, divine, or primal attacks, or attacks that rely
on magical prowess, which covers most spellcasting
enemies. If the attack is a recharge power, the target gains
it as an encounter power instead.
If the enemy has more than one option in one of
these categories, you learn all the choices and choose one
when you use this power.
New Level 16 Utility Spells

definitions.name: Bigger on the Inside
definitions.fullText:
Bigger on the Inside
Wizard Utility 16
You bend space itself in a contained area, so that those who ent
a tent find themselves in a full living room, and those who enter
an ordinary house find themselves in a multi
-story mansion.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Creation,
Stronghold
Standard Action
Melee touch
Requirement: You are inside a room with enough walls and
covered entrances, such as doors or tarps, that no one
outside has line of sight into it from any angle.
Target: The door or other covered entrance of the room you
are inside
Cast Time: 1 hour, 24 hours, or 1 week (see Effect).
Cost: 100 gp, 1,000 gp, or 10,000 gp (see Effect).
Effect: Roll an Arcana check. The inside of the target's room
expands, but its outside does not. You add squares to the
room's length, width, and height if it is roughly rectangular,
or to its radius and height if it is roughly circular, up to the
amount shown on the table below. For example, adding
20 squares turns a 4 -by-4 room into a 24 -by-24 room. The
added space takes up no more room in the building or
area around it, and it cannot be observed from outside the
room. The new walls, ceiling, and floor match the general
decor and patterns of the rest of the room, but nothing
else appears in the space unless you bring it in yourself.
The added squares count as magical zones.

definitions.name: Mage's Private Sanctum
definitions.fullText:
Mage's Private Sanctum
Wizard Utility 16
Let them press their ears to the wall. The wall has nothing to te
them.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Warding,
Stronghold
Standard Action
Close burst 5
Cast Time: 30 minutes.
Cost: 100 gp.
Effect: You ward either the burst or a single room you are
inside, giving it complete privacy for 24 hours. Scrying
powers and rituals cannot perceive anything inside the
area, and mind-reading effects do not work on creatures
inside it. Most sound cannot escape t he area, and
creatures outside it take a -15 penalty to Perception
checks to hear what is happening inside. A dark, foggy
mass surrounds the area, blocking sight into it from
outside, even for creatures with darkvision, while
creatures inside can see out n ormally. The ward does not
prevent anyone from walking into or out of the area.

definitions.fullText:
Dispel Disguise
Wizard Utility 22
The glamour breaks like a dropped mirror, and whatever was
hiding behind the face stands bare in the light.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Transmutation, Illusion,
Social
Immediate
Ranged 20
Reaction
Trigger: You succeed on an Insight check to recognize that a
creature is not its true self because of a magical disguise,
such as an illusion, shapeshifting, a charm, or a similar
transmutation or mind -altering effect.
Target: The disguised creature
Effect: You dispel the illusion, shapeshifting, or similar effect
on the target, so that everyone can see the target for who
it truly is.

definitions.name: Guardian Statues
definitions.fullText:
Guardian Statues
Wizard Utility 22
The gargoyles on the roof were always there. They were only
waiting to be asked.
Daily + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Creation,
Stronghold
Standard Action
Personal
Cast Time: 24 hours.
Effect: You add one guardian to your stronghold in the form
of a decorative, inanimate construct. Choose its type:
metallic (such as a suit of armor), flying (such as a
gargoyle), humanoid (such as a marble statue of a man, a
wax figure, or a brass statue of a rider on a horse), or
animal (such as a stone statue of a beast). You must
perform this ritual once for each guardian you create. A
stronghold can hold any combination of up to 4 guardians
if it is small (such as an inn), up to 8 if it is medium (such
as a castle), or up to 12 if it is large (such as a huge estate
and its grounds, or a military camp).
While your stronghold has at least one guardian
and you are on its grounds, you can use the Animate
Guardian Statues power.

powers.name: Church Sanctuary

definitions.name: Church Sanctuary
definitions.fullText:
Church Sanctuary
Cleric Utility 6
You have some influence within your church, and those friendly to
it, and are able to easily leverage it for food and shelter.
Daily + Non-Combat, Social, Urban
Minor Action
Personal
Target: One church, temple, shelter, shrine, etc. in the local
area for a deity of the same alignment as your deity
Effect: The target religious building will welcome you in with
open arms, letting you and your party stay there for free, and
feed you for free. They will also do their best to defend you if
you are being chased, stalked, or attacked. If the target
religious sanctuary is of your same deity, its caretakers will
work even harder to make you more comfortable, well -fed,
and well defended, and they will have a lower bar to help
you (perhaps even helping you if everyone else in an area is
unfriendly to you, for example).
DM Note: Whether they ask for something in return for this
service is up to the DM, but if the cleric uses this power, the
DM is encouraged to make sure they get the proper service
they requested first before owners try to parlay for a favor or
quest.

Black Eyes and Bloody
Fighter Utility 6
Nose (Fighter)
You hit an enemy in the face, not to cause any meaningful or letha
damage, but to cause some temporary superficial ugliness.

Melee Touch

positive appearance, it gets a -5 penalty.

Diplomacy or bluff), it only gets a -2 penalty.

Paladin Utility 2
Darkness
Your weapon emits an anti-light that extinguishes not only light, bu
hope, wherever it touches.

Target: One weapon, shield, or holy symbol you are touching.
Effect: The target spreads shadows from itself until the end of

do fully cover all light sources in a close burst 3 zone
centered on the target, cance ling out their light emitting

travels with the target object when it moves. You can dismiss
this effect as a free action at any time. Gain a +2 bonus to
Intimidate checks against enemies within th e shadows,
except shadow, undead, demons, or devil creatures, or those
resistant to necrotic damage.

definitions.name: Call Loyal Steed
definitions.fullText:
Call Loyal Steed
Paladin Utility 2
You gain the service of a loyal mount. With a whistle or a call, it
gallops to your location at great haste.
Daily + Non-Combat, Travel
Standard Action
Ranged 10
Requirement: You are taking a short rest.
Target: Each ally who is taking a rest with you. You cannot
target a creature who is targeted by or using another Rest
ability this turn.
Effect: Choose one of two effects when you use this power -
+
You convince a non -hostile creature of your level or
lower that has the mount keyword to bear you as a
rider. It can't already be loyal to anyone else. It
becomes the chosen mount loyal to you for this
power in the future. You can only have one loyal
mount with this power at a time. You can release a
mount currently loyal to you via this power from
your service as a free action by giving them to
someone else or releasing them in the wild.
+
Once you have chosen a loyal mount for this power,
you can use this power to call the mount to an
unoccupied square at the max range if not in
combat. If in combat, it arrives at the beginning of
your next turn at the edge of the battle map (or at
max range if using theater of the mind). Once it
arrives, it is an ally to you and it can act as a mount
for you or an ally you designate. It will follow your
commands, although it's still generally a normal
creature and the DM may rule that Nature checks
are required if your commands are complicated or
you aren't riding it. The only action the mount can
take while while riderless is free or move actions.

powers.name: Backup Plan Flashback (Short)

definitions.name: Backup Plan Flashback (Short)
definitions.fullText:
Backup Plan Flashback
Rogue Utility 22
(Short)
You spend the downtime asking the worst question you know:
what if it all goes wrong? By the time you move, every answer is
already in your pocket.
Daily + Non-Combat, Combat
Free Action
Personal
Requirement: You have the Planning the Operation power
and used it during a short rest.
Effect: The current scene is paused, and you trigger a short
flashback scene back to when you were making this plan
during the short rest in which you used Planning the
Operation. Establish in the fiction one bit of preparation
you and/or your PC allies made just in case you ran into
the present situation. It must be a limited change - one
that you could have accomplished in 5 or 10 minutes.
Afterwards, when you return back to the present scene, the
next attack roll, saving throw, skill check, or ability check
of you or an ally that benefits from the change you made
to the fiction gains a bonus equal to your Intelligence
modifier until the end of the encounter (or until 5 minutes
ends).

definitions.name: Animate Guardian Statues
definitions.fullText:
Animate Guardian Statues
Wizard Utility 22
The gargoyles on the roof were always there. They were only
waiting to be asked.
Encounter + Non-Combat, Arcane, Ritual, Stronghold,
War
Standard Action
Personal
Requirement: You are on the grounds of your stronghold,
and it has at least one guardian created by the Guardian
Statues power (Wizard 22).
Cast Time: 5 minutes.
Effect: You animate one or more of the guardian statues
protecting your stronghold or bastion. The guardians act
on their own under the DM's control, defending the area
and slowing down attackers. They generally fight
defensively and off-screen, pursuing no farther than the
edge of your grounds or territory; if their fight ever
matters, use the statistics below. All guardians are
immune to disease, poison, sleep, psychic damage, charm
effects, and other mind-affecting effects. A guardian can
turn back into a statue , gaining resist 40 to all damage
while it remains one.
Metallic Guardian: +50 hit points, +5 Fortitude, and +2 to
saving throws against ongoing damage. Resist 5 to all
damage except slashing damage, such as from blades. -2
speed and -2 Reflex. Melee attack: Intelligence vs. AC; 4d8
+ Intelligence modifier damage, and the target is knocked
prone.
Flying Guardian: +2 Fortitude and +2 Reflex. Resist 5 to all
damage except bludgeoning damage, such as from
hammers. Fly speed 8. Melee attack: Intelligence vs. AC;
2d8 + Intelligence modifier damage, and the guardian can
move up to 4 squares after the attack.
Humanoid Guardian: +10 hit points, +2 Fortitude, and +2
Will. Melee attack: Intelligence vs. AC; 1d10 + Intelligence

supportingRules.title: Advancement options and non-combat power rules
supportingRules.text:
5 
 
2. N EW R ULES FOR N ON -
C OMBAT U TILITY 
POWERS 
This book introduces rules to modify character develop-
ment by introducing a new axis of utility powers, combat 
and non-combat. All utility powers are divided into one of 
those two categories. This book will help by dividing all 
existing utility powers into one of these two categories and 
add new non -combat utility powers .  
If you add new homebrew powers, you can use 
the way existing powers are categorized to help you deter-
mine what category they should be in. 
MODIFIED CHARACTER 
ADVANCEMENT
 OPTION #1 
 
Modify character Level -Up rules as such: 
+ At level 2, characters will gain 2 utility powers 
instead of 1. They will select one Combat utility 
power and one Non -Combat utility power. 
+ At level 6, characters will chose either 1 Combat 
utility power, or 1 Non -Combat utility power. 
+ After that, they must choose from an alternating 
category each level they would gain a Utility 
power. 
+  In other words, if they chose a Combat Utility 
power at level 6, then at level 10 they choose a 
Non-Combat one, at level 16 they choose a Com-
bat one, and at level 22 they choose a Non -
Combat one. 
+ And thus, if they chose a Non -Combat Utility 
power at level 6, then at level 10 they must 
choose a Combat one, at level 16 they must 
choose a Non-Combat one, and at level 22 they 
must choose a Combat one.
 
+ You may retrain a Combat utility power to a 
Non-Combat utility power , or vice-versa. How-
ever, if you would do so and end up with 2 more 
powers in one category than another, you must 
retrain another power so the two end up either 
equal or with one category having only 1 more 
than the other.   
+ By level 22, you should have 3 from each cate-
gory, 6 total. 
 
DM NOTE ON SELECTING NON
-
COMBAT POWERS
 
While it is easy to predict that combat will be a part of 
any Dungeons & Dragons campaign, what non-combat 
aspects of a campaign can be widely disparate. As such, 
there are a couple of different philosophies to selecting 
these powers. You can also combine some of these, such 
as change the campaign based on player choices, unless 
they pick one that won’t work at all (such as overland 
travel power in a campaign taking place in a single city), 
in which case you can notify the player. 
1. Campaign First, No Communication : Players and 
DM’s don’t communicate about campaign themes, 
but players can always retrain non
-combat utility 
powers if they don’t find them useful. This is the most 
“realistic”. 
2. Campaign First, DM’s Help Players Choose: The 
DM’s give players an idea of some exploration and/or 
social challenges that can pop up during the 
campaign. Also, players run their non-combat utility 
power choices by the DM. 
3. DM Changes Campaign Based on Power Choices: 
The DM uses the non-combat player choices to get 
an idea of the kinds of things players will want to 
encounter or want their character to be good at, and 
the DM shapes their campaign to utilize these 
specialties. They don’t have to change the whole 
campaign, just try to pop up these kinds of challenges 
in it. 
 
UPDATED LEVEL UP TABLE FOR LEVELS 2, 6, 10, 16, AND 22
 (CHOOSE ONE PATH, LEFT OR RIGHT)
 
Level 
Combat -First Utility Power Path 
Non-Combat First Utility Power Path 
Level 2 
Gain 1 Combat utility power and 1 Non -Combat Utility Power 
Gain 1 Non -Combat utility power and 1 Combat 
utility power 
Level 6 
Gain 1 Combat utility power 
Gain 1 Non-Combat utility power 
Level 10 
Gain 1 Non -Combat Utility power 
Gain 1 Combat utility power 
Level 16 
 
Gain 1 Combat utility power 
Gain 1 Non -Combat utility power 
Level 22 
Gain 1 Non -Combat Utility power 
Gain 1 Combat utility power 

 
6 
 
ALTERNATIVE 
MODIFIED
 CHARACTER ADVANCEMENT
 OPTION #2 
You may also instead choose to use this simpler rule, but it will end with characters having even more 
powers than the rules on the previous page.
 Characters will have more capabilities in and out of combat than 
default characters of the same level, so you may want to keep that in mind.
 
 
 
If you prefer players having more choices, you can use the following rule instead:
 
+ Players choose to learn one Combat and one Non
-Combat utility power at levels 2, 6, 10, 16, and 22.
 As 
usual, you can replace one of these powers with a race or skill power, but must still be of the same category 
(Combat or Non -Combat). 
 
UPDATED LEVEL UP TABLE FOR LEVELS 2, 6, 10, 16, AND 22
 
Level 
Utility Power s 
Level 2 
Gain 1 Combat utility power and 1 Non
-Combat Utility Power 
Level 6 
Gain 1 Combat utility power and 1 Non
-Combat Utility Power 
Level 10 
Gain 1 Combat utility power and 1 Non
-Combat Utility Power 
Level 16 
 
Gain 1 Combat utility power and 1 Non
-Combat Utility Power 
Level 22 
Gain 1 Combat utility power and 1 Non
-Combat Utility Power 
 
 

 
7 
 
N EW R ULES FOR N ON -COMBAT U TILITY POWERS 
Ritual / Martial Practice Powers 
Some powers have the Ritual or Martial Practice 
keyword. Th ese are considered rituals
 or martial 
practices by other effects. In addition, they may share 
some similarities with rituals and martial practices.
 
 
They may have extended cast times like 
these 
effects usually do. If so, they will display, in addition to 
the normal actions of powers
, a cast time. Consider 
these cast times the amount of time the power has to be 
sustained, with a standard action used each round.
 
Naturally, these can be sustained past the normal limit 
of 5 minutes. 
 
Sometimes these ritual powers have 
component costs, although it is mu
ch rarer than 
normal rituals or martial practices. 
 
Rest Powers 
Some powers have the Rest keyword, and have a 
trigger that indicates that they must be performed 
during a rest. You can only use one of these Rest 
powers during each rest.  
The power itself will indicate what kind of rest 
it can be performed with.
 Generally, you can still spend 
healing surges to heal during a short rest as well as 
perform a rest power. 
 
Cantrip Powers 
Some powers have the Cantrip keyword. These 
indicate a type of harmless, non
-combat magical spell. 
All of the wizard powers gained through the 
Wizard cantrip feature now have this keyword, as well 
as various other similar 
powers that are given to other 
classes. 
 
Niche Powers 
Some powers I have given the category of “Niche”. 
These are Combat utility powers I have subjectively 
decided are weak or are strictly worse than another 
existing power by the same class
 and level (usually with 
the help of online optimization handbooks). Since I 
doubt they’d rarely be picked otherwise, I 
am 
considering letting players pick them instead of non
-
combat powers. You can consider it a house
-rule that is 
up to the DM to decide whether these categories count 
as both Combat and Non
-Combat utility powers, or as 
just Combat .  
The advantage to including these powers in 
Non -Combat Utility power lists is that it expands those 
lists slightly. The downside is that it 
allows players to 
pick what are technically combat powers for their Non
-
Combat Utility category.
 It’s up to the DM and players 
whether they care about this or not.
 
It also helps in that if a campaign is mostly 
combat -focused, it encourages players to pick some 
cool powers they’d be less inclined to pick normally.
 
 
If the reader of this document sees a Niche 
power they think is actually quite a bit more powerful 
or generally useful than I have estimated it as, let me 
know so I can remove th
is categorization from it for 
future versions of this document.

supportingRules.title: Quick and Dirty Combat
supportingRules.text:
8 
 
3. OPTIONAL N EW S UBSYSTEMS
 
 
QUICK AND D IRTY COMBAT 
There are many times when violence is the answer, 
but you would like to resolve 
combat very quickly. Not 
every fight deserves the whole process of rolling up 
initiatives, tracking conditions , and so on. Some fights 
are just not important in the scheme of things.
 
One new alternative we are presenting for these 
moments is the Quick and Dirty Combat rules. These 
are perfect for low -stakes, quick combat where speed is 
the primary desire. It can resolve a combat in one roll . 
 
 
Declare Outcome, Establish Order
 
First, t he player who initiates the combat
 
declare s their desired outcome. Examples include 
knock them out, escape, intimidate them into stop 
fighting, kill, etc.They initiate combat against the most 
powerful enemy in the grouop they are fighting.
 
The DM also decides what outcome the enemy 
wants. It can be to run away or stop the PC from 
proceeding, or even just to continue fighting.
 It may 
change at any point, too. 
Player and enemies must be close enough to 
interact with each other. Unless the PC is surprised, 
they then get to choose whether they are fighting 
offensively or defensively. If they are surprised, they 
must choose to fight defensively.
 
Roll for Attacks and Deal Damage 
Fighting Defensively
 
The enemy rolls to attack the player. If they 
hit, they deal 1 + half their level damage
 and 
successfully a ccomplish their goal. If they don’t, the PC 
accomplishes their goal.
 
 
Fighting Offensively 
 
The player rolls to attack the enemy
. If they 
hit, they get their desired outcome. If they miss, t
he 
enemy deals 4 + half their level damage
 and they 
accomplish their goal. 
Surprised 
 
If the PC is surprised, they must fight 
defensively, and the enemy gets a +2 bonus to their 
attack roll.  
 
If the enemy is surprised, the PC
 may roll 
twice for their attack roll and choose either result.
 
Finish the Scene 
If there are still enemies, to fight, you may 
continue the Quick and Dirty Combat with
 the same or 
another PC. 
Teamwork 
Enemy Teamwork - Multiple enemies add a +1 to 
the attack roll and a +1 to the defense for each two 
enemies participating. If the PC wins, their desired 
outcome applies to all participating enemies.
 
Ally Teamwork - Allies can also choose to aid the 
roll . Each ally who helps, whether they succeed their 
roll or not, takes all of the damage from the enemies in 
addition to the initiating player
, so there is risk in 
getting involved in the scuffle.
 
+ Fighting Offensively
 – Each helping ally
 
rolls their own attacks. For each 
allied 
player who hits, add a +2 to the attack roll 
of the initiating playe r. 
+ Fighting Defensively
 – Each helping ally
 
roll an Aid Another skill check against
 an 
Easy DC of the enemy’s level.
 They may 
use any skill that is relevant, usually 
Acrobatics or Endurance (
maybe a 
Monster Knowledge check). For each ally 
who succeeds, add a +2 bonus to the 
initiating player’s defenses. 
Enemy Stats to Use 
If you don’t have the stats of the enemy you are doing 
Quick and Dirty Combat with available, simply use 
these stats: 
Attack : level + 5  
Damage:  
+ Half level + 
4 (fighting offensively)
 
+ Half level + 1 (fighting defensively)
 
AC Defense: level + 15  
Non -AC Defense: level + 13
 
Aid Another DC: Easy DC of level (you can 
approximate this with half level + 8)
 
 
 

 
9 
 
 
WAYS TO DO QUICK COMBAT
 
D&D 4th Edition tends to be better when you save the 
full force of its tactical combat for actually dramatic and 
dangerous fights. There are a few alternatives when 
trying to resolve an unimportant,  not dramatic, or not as 
dangerous battle quickly: 
+ 
One is to use normal combat rules but make 
every enemy a minion. (This is the main way to 
make quick combats now, although we propose 
making the Quick and Dirty Combat rules the 
main way.) 
+ 
Another is to use a skill challenge, which is 
good for extended scenes which are dramatic 
but not dangeorus. (A good example is a tavern 
brawl or fighting through a violent
, peasant mob.) 
+ 
One new alternative we are presenting is for 
these Quick and Dirty Combat rules. These are 
perfect for low -stakes, quick combat where 
speed is the primary desire. 
There are less 
attack rolls involved, so it resolves in the 
player’s favor more often than the first option. 
(Examples include taking out a bouncer at the 
bar, knocking out an unexpected mooks in a 
stealth infilitration mission, or if you need to take 
out multiple waves of guards on your way to see
the king like in The Two Towers.) 
 
 
HANDLING 
BIG GROUPS OF
 
ENEMIES IN QUICK AND DIRTY 
COMBAT 
If there are too many enemies but you still 
want to make it possible to win, it
’s recommended 
you do one of two things: 
+ Split the enemies into groups and 
have the players roll against each 
group, or  
+ Expand the number of enemies that 
are required to give the bonus (such 
as, every 3 or 4 enemies that give a 
+1).  
 
If splitting the enemies into groups, it’s 
recommended that you not use more than 6 
enemies in a group this way, depending on how 
many bonuses your players have to their attack 
rolls and how low the enemy defense is
, you 
probably don’t want to give them more than a +3
 
to their bonuses. 
As for which to use, that depends on the feel 
the DM is going for in the scene. Sometimes it’s 
cool if one high level player takes out a whole 
gang in an ally in one quick scuffle of a roll. 
 
Other times, they may prefer to split up the 
groups to give each player a chance to shine (like 
in Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers, when some 
characters were taking out palace guards in the 
background 2 -3 at a time while the spotlight fell 
on Gandalf’s a ttempt to break the spell).

supportingRules.title: Renown
supportingRules.text:
10 
 
R ENOWN 
Renown is how well known a character is to the 
general public and how far their story has spread.
 
 
Using Renown 
 
DM’s can start tracking this from the beginning, or they 
can start tracking it from any point in the campaign. 
Some logical places to start are when characters start 
leaving their initial immediate area, for example, or for 
when they hit certain level milestones (level 5 and level 
10 are common ones). 
 
The important part is that how Renown is used is 
flexible, and it is up to the players and the DM
 and the 
narrative they have developed:
 
• 
It's more important in a campaign that is more 
centered on the players being movers and 
shakers, people of influence (examples include 
political campaigns, war campaigns, they are 
talking to kings, raising armies, maneuvering 
factions, etc).  
o 
Examples include Game of Thrones, 
Aragon, Merry, Pippin, and Gandalf's 
journeys in Lord of the Rings, Chronicles 
of Narnia, and many campaigns like Red 
Hand of Doom (3.5), Reavers of 
Harkenwold (4e), or Tyranny of 
Dragons/Ride of Tiamat (5e). 
• 
It's less important in a campaign more 
centered on the adventure itself than on the 
patrons and influencing large amounts of 
people (examples include dungeon crawlers, 
heists, killing the local vampire lord, they are 
more focused on the quest itself and ho
w will 
they accomplish it, and individuals rather than 
groups of people).  
o 
Media examples include Frodo and Sam's 
journeys in Lord of the Rings, the Dresden 
Files, most fairy tales, Vox Machina 
(season 1), and many standard 
adventures like the Village of Homlet, 
Dungeon of the Mad Mage, or Curse of 
Strahd. 
 
Traveling vs Stationary Campaign 
 
If it's a traveling campaign, renown 
can help 
keep t rack of how well known they are outside the 
local area. The DM should feel free to l
imit how much 
it can increase in the local are
a, then lift that limit as 
they leave. 
 
If it's a stationary campaign, renown tracks how 
well known they are in the local setting
. You will have 
to separate the city either into different 
sections and 
districts, cultures and classes, or
 into different factions 
and renown will determine who well you are known 
outside of your initial block, district, class, faction, etc 
(this implies a city or town big enough to have those).
 
 
 
Earning Renown 
 
Renown is a numerical value that starts at 0.
 The DM 
may increase it by 1 for each character whenever they 
complete a quest or mission, or do something heroic, 
usually when they report back their success at the end 
of an adventure. It’s okay if some players have more or 
less renown than others. 
 
The DM is free to adjust this rate depending on the 
nature of the adventure and how well known they want 
the players to be. A faster rate implies that they assume 
leadership positions in the world quicker.
 
 
If they introduced renown later in the story, or it 
becomes more important later, than the DM may also 
elect to change the rate. They may start the campaign 
without tracking renown, for example, and then later 
decide as the campaign shifts focus to implement it, 
and gradually increase the rate as you head towards the 
final battle. 
 
 
Mechanical Benefits of Renown 
 
Renown can offer the the following benefits
 to players . 
 
1. Influencing Negotiation Skill Challenges.
 
2. Attracting Followers  
3. Optional DM Perks
 
 
Influencing Negotiation Skill Challenges
 
 
When trying to influence people of a certain rank or 
standing, being important or famous yourself can go a 
long way to help.  When your renown matches the 
impression level of the NPC, you gain a +2 bonus when 
interacting with them , depending on the nature of your 
fame. The DM may also choose to lower the number of 
successes required by 2
 (instead of, or in addition to, 
the skill check bonus).
 
 
For example, if the NPC inspires admire you, it may 
apply to Diplomacy checks. If you are more infamous 
than famous, than it may apply to Intimidation checks.
 
 
  

 
11 
 
You can apply these bonuses to other social 
skill checks as well, but we are working off of the 
assumption it can be a pain to check this chart for 
every little social check. 
 There is no need to stop the 
narrative so you an consult a chart to convince the 
bouncer to let you in the bar
 or the guard to let you in 
the town .  
On the other hand, social skill challenges
 are 
usually used when the social encounter 
are important 
and have a bigger spotlight on them
, or the request is 
too big to put on a single check.
 
 
IMPRESSION CHART 
Renown for 
Impression
 
Example NPC’s
 
1 - 2 
Starting area commoner
 
3 - 4 
Brigand leader, shop 
owner 
5 – 6 
Knight, local 
guildmaster 
7 – 8 
Professor, local known 
mage 
9 – 10 
Cult leader, noble lord
 
11 – 13 
Assassin, locally famous 
entertainer 
14 – 16 
Not local commoners, 
baron 
17 – 20 
Watch captain in large 
city, high priest, viscount
 
21 – 23 
Count, warlord 
24 – 26 
Marquis, world -
renowned entertainer 
27 – 30 
Duke, spymaster 
31 - 33 
Archmage, prince 
34 - 36 
Monarch 
37 – 40 
Demon lord 
41 – 45 
Archdevil, archfey, 
demigod 
46 – 50 
Deity, titan 
 
 
Attracting Followers 
 
This is benefit is mostly useful if the characters have a 
stronghold of some type, but the DM can also apply this 
benefit to renown if you would like to 
add to the 
number of retainers, fans, allies, or contacts players 
have. 
 
Renown 
Number of Followers
 
10 
1 
20 
2 
30 
3 
40 
4 
50 
5 
 
Types of Followers 
 
+ Artisans – They make or grow things
 
+ Sages – They research or write things
 
+ Soldiers – They fight, spy, or protect things. 
They protect teh law in your area, may lead or 
captain your units. Rettainers are usually 
these. 
+ Armies /units – Masses of faceless soldiers 
purely for defending the stronghold
 (if you are 
using the warfare subsystem).
 
+ Ambassadors – They talk or deliver messages. 
Can help attract units from other lands or 
ancestries, can help improve attitudes when 
speaking to leaders of other domains, 
organizations, kingdoms, etc.
 
+ Special Allies – Special allies rolled 
on that 
don’t work for you, and may even be stronger 
than you, but your interests align in some way 
(dragons, giants, etc.). 
+ Contacts – Someone you know who exists to 
provide information on an area, person, etc
 (“I 
know a guy”). 
 
Other Optional Perks for Renown 
 
The DM is free to add other 
mechanical perks for 
having higher renown. Often, additional perks use the 
faction renown system, and the benefits come with 
being part of a faction or having a high reputation for a 
faction. 
Some examples include discounts at shops (maybe 
for advertising their product, like a sponsorship)
, gifts, 
random help and other resources.
 
 
Narrative Benefits of Renown 
 
The DM is also encouraged to use the renown as a good 
reference for how famous the players are in the 
narrative. Some examples of 
additional benefits 
include : 
1. Gaining access to important people
 
2. Gaining access to new exclusive places  
3. Random people in the narrative will know the 
PC’s names, though it can also make it harder 
to avoid notice 
4. Political influe nce, including being able to 
wield more power in organizations they are a 
part of 
5. They may receive higher level quests
 
 
 
 

 
12 
 
 
Specific Types of Renown 
 
In additoin to using this base renown to represent their 
general reputation among the populace, you can also 
track more specific types of renown.
 
Area Renown
 – It’s possible that when traveling to 
areas that are extremely separated that the PC’s 
previously accrued renown has no effect (the “I’m big

renown track in this new area. Examples may include if 
the players travel to a different continent, dimensional 
plane, or the DM may institute this for isolated pockets 
of civilization, such as an island or with a tribe in
 a 
dense forest.

 – The DM may also choose to 
have the players track their reputation with different 
factions instead of or in addition to their general 
renown.

different kinds of 
followers that may appear at your stronghold and what 
benfeits they can provide ,  you can look at the

2. N EW R ULES FOR N ON -
C OMBAT U TILITY 
POWERS 
This book introduces rules to modify character develop-
ment by introducing a new axis of utility powers, combat 
and non-combat. All utility powers are divided into one of 
those two categories. This book will help by dividing all 
existing utility powers into one of these two categories and 
add new non -combat utility powers .  
If you add new homebrew powers, you can use 
the way existing powers are categorized to help you deter-
mine what category they should be in. 
MODIFIED CHARACTER 
ADVANCEMENT
 OPTION #1 
 
Modify character Level -Up rules as such: 
+ At level 2, characters will gain 2 utility powers 
instead of 1. They will select one Combat utility 
power and one Non -Combat utility power. 
+ At level 6, characters will chose either 1 Combat 
utility power, or 1 Non -Combat utility power. 
+ After that, they must choose from an alternating 
category each level they would gain a Utility 
power. 
+  In other words, if they chose a Combat Utility 
power at level 6, then at level 10 they choose a 
Non-Combat one, at level 16 they choose a Com-
bat one, and at level 22 they choose a Non -
Combat one. 
+ And thus, if they chose a Non -Combat Utility 
power at level 6, then at level 10 they must 
choose a Combat one, at level 16 they must 
choose a Non-Combat one, and at level 22 they 
must choose a Combat one.
 
+ You may retrain a Combat utility power to a 
Non-Combat utility power , or vice-versa. How-
ever, if you would do so and end up with 2 more 
powers in one category than another, you must 
retrain another power so the two end up either 
equal or with one category having only 1 more 
than the other.   
+ By level 22, you should have 3 from each cate-
gory, 6 total. 
 
DM NOTE ON SELECTING NON
-
COMBAT POWERS
 
While it is easy to predict that combat will be a part of 
any Dungeons & Dragons campaign, what non-combat 
aspects of a campaign can be widely disparate. As such, 
there are a couple of different philosophies to selecting 
these powers. You can also combine some of these, such 
as change the campaign based on player choices, unless 
they pick one that won’t work at all (such as overland 
travel power in a campaign taking place in a single city), 
in which case you can notify the player. 
1. Campaign First, No Communication : Players and 
DM’s don’t communicate about campaign themes, 
but players can always retrain non
-combat utility 
powers if they don’t find them useful. This is the most 
“realistic”. 
2. Campaign First, DM’s Help Players Choose: The 
DM’s give players an idea of some exploration and/or 
social challenges that can pop up during the 
campaign. Also, players run their non-combat utility 
power choices by the DM. 
3. DM Changes Campaign Based on Power Choices: 
The DM uses the non-combat player choices to get 
an idea of the kinds of things players will want to 
encounter or want their character to be good at, and 
the DM shapes their campaign to utilize these 
specialties. They don’t have to change the whole 
campaign, just try to pop up these kinds of challenges 
in it.

N EW R ULES FOR N ON -COMBAT U TILITY POWERS 
Ritual / Martial Practice Powers 
Some powers have the Ritual or Martial Practice 
keyword. Th ese are considered rituals
 or martial 
practices by other effects. In addition, they may share 
some similarities with rituals and martial practices.
 
 
They may have extended cast times like 
these 
effects usually do. If so, they will display, in addition to 
the normal actions of powers
, a cast time. Consider 
these cast times the amount of time the power has to be 
sustained, with a standard action used each round.
 
Naturally, these can be sustained past the normal limit 
of 5 minutes. 
 
Sometimes these ritual powers have 
component costs, although it is mu
ch rarer than 
normal rituals or martial practices. 
 
Rest Powers 
Some powers have the Rest keyword, and have a 
trigger that indicates that they must be performed 
during a rest. You can only use one of these Rest 
powers during each rest.  
The power itself will indicate what kind of rest 
it can be performed with.
 Generally, you can still spend 
healing surges to heal during a short rest as well as 
perform a rest power. 
 
Cantrip Powers 
Some powers have the Cantrip keyword. These 
indicate a type of harmless, non
-combat magical spell. 
All of the wizard powers gained through the 
Wizard cantrip feature now have this keyword, as well 
as various other similar 
powers that are given to other 
classes. 
 
Niche Powers 
Some powers I have given the category of “Niche”. 
These are Combat utility powers I have subjectively 
decided are weak or are strictly worse than another 
existing power by the same class
 and level (usually with 
the help of online optimization handbooks). Since I 
doubt they’d rarely be picked otherwise, I 
am 
considering letting players pick them instead of non
-
combat powers. You can consider it a house
-rule that is 
up to the DM to decide whether these categories count 
as both Combat and Non
-Combat utility powers, or as 
just Combat .  
The advantage to including these powers in 
Non -Combat Utility power lists is that it expands those 
lists slightly. The downside is that it 
allows players to 
pick what are technically combat powers for their Non
-
Combat Utility category.
 It’s up to the DM and players 
whether they care about this or not.
 
It also helps in that if a campaign is mostly 
combat -focused, it encourages players to pick some 
cool powers they’d be less inclined to pick normally.
 
 
If the reader of this document sees a Niche 
power they think is actually quite a bit more powerful 
or generally useful than I have estimated it as, let me 
know so I can remove th
is categorization from it for 
future versions of this document.

3. OPTIONAL N EW S UBSYSTEMS
 
 
QUICK AND D IRTY COMBAT 
There are many times when violence is the answer, 
but you would like to resolve 
combat very quickly. Not 
every fight deserves the whole process of rolling up 
initiatives, tracking conditions , and so on. Some fights 
are just not important in the scheme of things.
 
One new alternative we are presenting for these 
moments is the Quick and Dirty Combat rules. These 
are perfect for low -stakes, quick combat where speed is 
the primary desire. It can resolve a combat in one roll . 
 
 
Declare Outcome, Establish Order
 
First, t he player who initiates the combat
 
declare s their desired outcome. Examples include 
knock them out, escape, intimidate them into stop 
fighting, kill, etc.They initiate combat against the most 
powerful enemy in the grouop they are fighting.
 
The DM also decides what outcome the enemy 
wants. It can be to run away or stop the PC from 
proceeding, or even just to continue fighting.
 It may 
change at any point, too. 
Player and enemies must be close enough to 
interact with each other. Unless the PC is surprised, 
they then get to choose whether they are fighting 
offensively or defensively. If they are surprised, they 
must choose to fight defensively.
 
Roll for Attacks and Deal Damage 
Fighting Defensively
 
The enemy rolls to attack the player. If they 
hit, they deal 1 + half their level damage
 and 
successfully a ccomplish their goal. If they don’t, the PC 
accomplishes their goal.
 
 
Fighting Offensively 
 
The player rolls to attack the enemy
. If they 
hit, they get their desired outcome. If they miss, t
he 
enemy deals 4 + half their level damage
 and they 
accomplish their goal. 
Surprised 
 
If the PC is surprised, they must fight 
defensively, and the enemy gets a +2 bonus to their 
attack roll.  
 
If the enemy is surprised, the PC
 may roll 
twice for their attack roll and choose either result.
 
Finish the Scene 
If there are still enemies, to fight, you may 
continue the Quick and Dirty Combat with
 the same or 
another PC. 
Teamwork 
Enemy Teamwork - Multiple enemies add a +1 to 
the attack roll and a +1 to the defense for each two 
enemies participating. If the PC wins, their desired 
outcome applies to all participating enemies.
 
Ally Teamwork - Allies can also choose to aid the 
roll . Each ally who helps, whether they succeed their 
roll or not, takes all of the damage from the enemies in 
addition to the initiating player
, so there is risk in 
getting involved in the scuffle.
 
+ Fighting Offensively
 – Each helping ally
 
rolls their own attacks. For each 
allied 
player who hits, add a +2 to the attack roll 
of the initiating playe r. 
+ Fighting Defensively
 – Each helping ally
 
roll an Aid Another skill check against
 an 
Easy DC of the enemy’s level.
 They may 
use any skill that is relevant, usually 
Acrobatics or Endurance (
maybe a 
Monster Knowledge check). For each ally 
who succeeds, add a +2 bonus to the 
initiating player’s defenses. 
Enemy Stats to Use 
If you don’t have the stats of the enemy you are doing 
Quick and Dirty Combat with available, simply use 
these stats: 
Attack : level + 5  
Damage:  
+ Half level + 
4 (fighting offensively)
 
+ Half level + 1 (fighting defensively)
 
AC Defense: level + 15  
Non -AC Defense: level + 13
 
Aid Another DC: Easy DC of level (you can 
approximate this with half level + 8)

WAYS TO DO QUICK COMBAT
 
D&D 4th Edition tends to be better when you save the 
full force of its tactical combat for actually dramatic and 
dangerous fights. There are a few alternatives when 
trying to resolve an unimportant,  not dramatic, or not as 
dangerous battle quickly: 
+ 
One is to use normal combat rules but make 
every enemy a minion. (This is the main way to 
make quick combats now, although we propose 
making the Quick and Dirty Combat rules the 
main way.) 
+ 
Another is to use a skill challenge, which is 
good for extended scenes which are dramatic 
but not dangeorus. (A good example is a tavern 
brawl or fighting through a violent
, peasant mob.) 
+ 
One new alternative we are presenting is for 
these Quick and Dirty Combat rules. These are 
perfect for low -stakes, quick combat where 
speed is the primary desire. 
There are less 
attack rolls involved, so it resolves in the 
player’s favor more often than the first option. 
(Examples include taking out a bouncer at the 
bar, knocking out an unexpected mooks in a 
stealth infilitration mission, or if you need to take 
out multiple waves of guards on your way to see
the king like in The Two Towers.) 
 
 
HANDLING 
BIG GROUPS OF
 
ENEMIES IN QUICK AND DIRTY 
COMBAT 
If there are too many enemies but you still 
want to make it possible to win, it
’s recommended 
you do one of two things: 
+ Split the enemies into groups and 
have the players roll against each 
group, or  
+ Expand the number of enemies that 
are required to give the bonus (such 
as, every 3 or 4 enemies that give a 
+1).  
 
If splitting the enemies into groups, it’s 
recommended that you not use more than 6 
enemies in a group this way, depending on how 
many bonuses your players have to their attack 
rolls and how low the enemy defense is
, you 
probably don’t want to give them more than a +3
 
to their bonuses. 
As for which to use, that depends on the feel 
the DM is going for in the scene. Sometimes it’s 
cool if one high level player takes out a whole 
gang in an ally in one quick scuffle of a roll. 
 
Other times, they may prefer to split up the 
groups to give each player a chance to shine (like 
in Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers, when some 
characters were taking out palace guards in the 
background 2 -3 at a time while the spotlight fell 
on Gandalf’s a ttempt to break the spell).

speed is the primary desire.
There are less
attack rolls involved, so it resolves in the
player’s favor more often than the first option.
(Examples include taking out a bouncer at the
bar, knocking out an unexpected mooks in a
stealth infilitration mission, or if you need to take
out multiple waves of guards on your way to see
the king like in The Two Towers.)
HANDLING
BIG GROUPS OF
ENEMIES IN QUICK AND DIRTY
COMBAT
If there are too many enemies but you still
want to make it possible to win, it
’s recommended
you do one of two things:
+ Split the enemies into groups and
have the players roll against each
group, or
+ Expand the number of enemies that
are required to give the bonus (such
as, every 3 or 4 enemies that give a
+1).
If splitting the enemies into groups, it’s
recommended that you not use more than 6
enemies in a group this way, depending on how
many bonuses your players have to their attack
rolls and how low the enemy defense is
, you
probably don’t want to give them more than a +3
to their bonuses.
As for which to use, that depends on the feel
the DM is going for in the scene. Sometimes it’s
cool if one high level player takes out a whole
gang in an ally in one quick scuffle of a roll.
Other times, they may prefer to split up the
groups to give each player a chance to shine (like
in Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers, when some
characters were taking out palace guards in the
background 2 -3 at a time while the spotlight fell
on Gandalf’s a ttempt to break the spell).
